From Support Function to Strategic Partner - An Organizational-Sociological Study of Collaboration Barriers Between IT and Business at Danish Crown
Semi-parametric multi-type Markov point processes
projects.abstract:
This project introduces spatial point processes with a particular focus on modelling and inference for semiparametric multitype Markov point processes. The main goal is to model large-scale spatial variation as well as local dependence between prehospital emergency resource types using the Papangelou conditional intensity, allowing the intensity to depend on spatial covariates and local interaction structures.
Inference is carried out using the conditional pseudo-likelihood, which circumvents the intractable normalizing constant of the full likelihood. Under suitable regularity conditions, the resulting estimator is consistent and asymptotically normal despite the presence of spatial dependence. The methodology is applied to a dataset of prehospital emergency incidents in the North Denmark Region. The analysis demonstrates how the semiparametric model captures spatial heterogeneity and local interaction effects while also investigating geographical or demographic variation in the disposition of prehospital emergency resource types.

projects.title: When Accessibility Meets Practice A Discourse-Analytical Thesis
projects.abstract:
This thesis explores how the meaning of accessibility is constructed and negotiated within Danish municipal mental health treatment services for young people in psychological distress. The study focuses on the newly established “easily accessible” municipal treatment services introduced as part of the Danish psychiatric reform, which aims to ensure prevention, easy access to support, and psychological treatment for children and adolescents experiencing mental distress. Through a discourse analysis inspired by Ernesto Laclau and Chantal Mouffe’s discourse theory, the thesis examines how accessibility is constructed within both political documents and professional practice, and how tensions emerge between political ambitions and professional assessments in practice. The empirical material consists of a document analysis of the national guideline Professional Frameworks for Municipal Treatment Services for Children and Adolescents in Psychological Distress as well as two semi-structured interviews with professionals working within the treatment services. The results show that accessibility is politically constructed as a low-threshold principle emphasizing visibility, rapid access, and easily available support both physically and digitally. However, the analysis also demonstrates that accessibility in practice becomes closely connected to professional assessments, organizational limitations, and the need to define and delimit the target group. As a result, a tension emerges between the political ambition of easy access and the professional responsibility to assess whether young people should instead be referred to psychiatric services.
The thesis argues that accessibility cannot be understood as a neutral organizational principle, but rather as a discursive construction shaped through ongoing negotiations between political ambitions, professional knowledge, and organizational conditions. Furthermore, the study highlights how municipal treatment services simultaneously function as supportive welfare initiatives and as mechanisms of regulation that define which forms of psychological distress are recognized as eligible for treatment.

projects.title: A bit more than nothing
projects.abstract:
This thesis investigates how a knowledge bank, a shared digital repository for preserving and transferring operational and pedagogical knowledge, can be facilitated in an organization experiencing recurring knowledge loss due to high staff turnover, and what design principles emerge through that process. The empirical context is Greve Ungdomsskole, a Danish municipal youth school where seasonal employment structures mean that instructors regularly leave the organization, taking with them practical and pedagogical knowledge that is not systematically retained.

The study employs a Design-Based Research methodology, drawing on the author's prior experience as an instructor at the organization. Two iterative design cycles were carried out in collaboration with key organizational actors: a full-time employed staff member who initiated the brainstorming and planning of the knowledge bank, an administrative employee who assumed the role of system owner, and the youth school leader who provided organizational mandate. The digital product is a knowledge bank established in Microsoft Teams, with a team-specific handover template as its central artifact in this project.

The theoretical framework combines Nonaka’s theory of organizational knowledge creation, Davenport and Prusak’s conceptualization of knowledge as situated between data and judgment, and Schein’s process consultation model. These are applied predominantly retrospectively as interpretive lenses rather than as prescriptive design frameworks.

The analysis is organized into four different thematics. The first examines how the knowledge bank's design emerged as a response to knowledge loss, tracing the movement from initial brainstorming to a concrete artifact shaped by successive negotiations between different organizational perspectives. The second explores an unintended double function of the handover template: Designed as a practical handover tool, it was read by the school leader as a source of insight into instructors' pedagogical reasoning and professional values, revealing a latent organizational need for visibility into teaching practice. The third analyzes the facilitation process itself, showing how the researcher’s role moved between expert-oriented and process-consultative positions across different meetings and design phases. The fourth examines the transition from facilitator-driven process to organizational ownership, identifying signs of convergence around the design principle of manageability over completeness.

Three design principles emerged empirically from the process: manageability over completeness, employee-driven content, and gradual implementation. Additionally, a prioritization decision established team-specific knowledge as the first area of implementation. These principles are context-bound and cannot be directly generalized, but may serve as experience-based orientation points for similar design processes in comparable organizational contexts.

The thesis contributes to organizational knowledge management by documenting the concrete facilitation process involved in establishing a knowledge retention system, an aspect that receives less attention in the reviewed contributions on knowledge loss.

projects.title: Covert Identification of Analog FPV Drones
projects.abstract: We consider the problem of distinguishing between friendly analog FPV drones of identical model and components using their emitted video signal. In scenarios where encountered drones are not exclusively hostile, current counter-drone solution lacks ways of distinguishing between friendly and hostile drones. However, since adversary drone operators face the same identification challenge, we consider solutions that asymmetrically enable friendly identification while keeping adversary identification difficult. Two solution approaches are considered in the thesis. Firstly, we investigate if the hardware tolerances in the video-related components, produce viable distinctive features in the video signal. We analyzed FPV components and found that the most prominent difference was the carrier frequency offset (CFO) where ∼5-15 kHz separation between video transmitters was observed. While, promising for identification in theory, the CFOs were highly temperature-dependent, which lead to deeming the approach infeasible to extend to a practical solution. Secondly, we propose injecting a hidden identification signal in friendly drones’ video signal. We derive a generalized matched filter and evaluate performance on gathered FPV drone recordings. Under large amounts of transmission noise, (SNR of 10 dB relative to the video signal), the ROC curve of the detector had an AUC of 0.9997, and at a false alarm of 10−6 the detection probability was 75%.

projects.title: Cargo Placement as MINLP
projects.abstract: This project is about the placement of rolling cargo on Roll–On/Roll–Off ships. The modeling of a ship hull using NURBS curves and locally using 2nd degree polynomials is reviewed. How the ship is angled in relation to the rest of the world is described as a function of the placement of cargo and is calculated using integrals. It is described how integrals are found for the necessary curves, both numerically using the Gauss–Legendre approximation, and symbolically. The angles are approximated to the first degree. An algorithm is then designed to place cargo in order to minimize the angles, after which it is tested. The algorithm is shown to fail in up to 53% of cases, and the reasons for this are discussed.

projects.title: Pharmacometrics: The Modeling of Medicinal Treatments and Their Effects
projects.abstract: This project introduces the reader to the field of pharmacometrics through motivated definitions and theoretical results, which are afterwards applied to real-world trial data from Novo Nordisk. In order to model how a human body acts on a substance administered into the body, the pharmacokinetic model known as the linear compartment model, which can be described by matrix differential equations and Fick's law, is constructed. Multiple dosing (daily and weekly) is investigated through matrix derivations. To study how the drug affects the body, the E-max model from pharmacodynamics is derived. The theory of recurrent event analysis and the Andersen-Gill model is introduced. Non-linear mixed effect models and the first-order conditional estimation with interaction method is motivated for the estimation of parameters of compartment models in a population. Data provided by Novo Nordisk is analyzed using the theory, and, using statistical inference, it is shown that semaglutide treatment reduces the three-month average blood sugar levels and the risk for major adverse cardiovascular events in adults with type 2 diabetes.

projects.title: Child Centered Violence Prevention
Neural Network Methods for Gas Storage Valuation
projects.abstract: This thesis examines the valuation of natural gas storage contracts as a stochastic dynamic optimisation problem, comparing six continuation value approximation methods within the Least Squares Monte Carlo framework: polynomial OLS regression, spline regression, and nodewise and joint-input variants of the multi-layer perceptron (MLP) and the Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (KAN). Spot price dynamics are modelled using a one-factor mean-reverting model calibrated to Trading Hub Europe prices, and the framework is applied to the Danish storage system of Gas Storage Denmark (GSD) and a stylised Dutch salt cavern. Polynomial OLS and spline regression outperform both neural network approaches in the configurations studied. For the GSD case, OLS yields €123.481M while the best neural network, the joint-input MLP, reaches €107.101M, constituting a gap of approximately 13%. The near-affine inventory dependence of the continuation value favours polynomial regression and limits the benefit of larger networks. The study is limited by the one-factor price model, neural network training cost, and the computational inefficiency of the nodewise KAN, which is slower than OLS by a factor of roughly 600. Overall, the results indicate that classical LSMC with polynomial regression is both more accurate and orders of magnitude faster than neural network alternatives for the class of gas storage problems studied.

projects.title: MORPHEUS - A modular fixed wing drone platform for military use
projects.abstract: This project investigates how a modular fixed wing drone platform can support faster assembly, payload integration, rebuilding, and local manufacturing within the Danish Jaeger Corps. Current drone workflows rely heavily on manual integration and externally sourced platforms, limiting scalability and operational flexibility. The project followed an iterative and user-centered design process developed through continuous collaboration with the Jaeger Corps. Interviews, prototype evaluations, testing, and user feedback were used to identify challenges related to balancing, payload integration, manufacturability, and mission adaptability. The resulting concept, MORPHEUS, is a modular drone platform built around a standardized fuselage with interchangeable wings, tails, lids, payload protection systems, and an internal rail-and-plate mounting system. The platform enables rapid reconfiguration of internal components without redesigning the airframe. The project establishes a foundation for continued development and demonstrates the potential of modular drone architectures for scalable and adaptable military drone deployment.

projects.title: Multimodal Learning for Understanding and Classifying Stress
projects.abstract:
Understanding and reliably classifying human stress remains a significant challenge, primarily due to its high individual baseline variability, the disconnect between subjective and objective metrics, and the differences in elicitation protocols. To address these challenges, this thesis introduces two multimodal stress identification models: TempFeat, which utilizes features, and 3SI, which leverages self-supervised learning. Furthermore, we propose Synergy Identification via Network Clustering (SINC), a novel, model-agnostic explainable artificial intelligence framework designed to interpret these complex systems.

Evaluations show that the 3SI architecture achieves superior generalization, outperforming the state-of-the-art ADAPT model by at least 22.2% in balanced accuracy and 13.6% in weighted F1 score on unseen subjects. Furthermore, applying SINC to these models yielded insights into their decision making processes: SINC revealed that 3SI’s strong performance is driven by its ability to capture complex, cross-modal audiovisual interactions, whereas TempFeat primarily relies on intra-modal dependencies.

projects.title: Domesticating the institution: Transforming Skansevejens Skole into a Residential Care Home
projects.abstract:
This thesis explores a deinstitutionalization of the Residential Care Home and Social & Activity Center for people with cognitive and/or physical disabilities through a sustainable preservation-oriented transformation of Skansevejens Skole located in Nørresundby, Denmark. The project explores a domestication of the institution creating a social inclusive environment that enhances the users´ autonomy and revitalizes the area in relation to the surrounding context

Through an identification of user needs and investigations of life cycle assessment and daylight simulations the project sets its foundation in creating a sustainable inclusive design while respecting the social, historical and architectural value of the original building.

projects.title: Bringing Care Home: Rethinking senior and elderly care in small communities
projects.abstract:
This master thesis project is an exploration of a transformation of two poorly maintained buildings respectively from 1967 and 1975 on the Danish island, Læsø. The buildings are part of an already ongoing development plan of renovating the care home on Læsø and creating more senior housing.

The design transforms unremarkable rental units into modern and communal transitional housing for seniors and elderly offering varying degrees of privacy and opportunities for activity. Through an open and intuitive building layout in combination with dignified integrated care elements, users can age in their own homes - even as their need for assistance grows. With a special respect for the existing buildings and the surrounding environment, the homes blend into Læsø through their scale, architectural expression, and material references to both Læsø’s natural landscape and the buildings’ original construction period.

Another significant part of this thesis is the hypothesis that it may be beneficial and relevant to transform the existing buildings rather than demolish them and build entirely new developments, as is currently planned for the properties. Based on several parameters including operational energy, environmental impact, and architectural qualities, this thesis therefore examines, how to optimally transform the existing buildings, and finally compares this thesis’s proposal with the contractor’s presumed plans for the area.

Through an integrated design process, the project has been developed through iterative design phases, parallel problem-solving proposals, and theoretical perspectives. Regarding the latter, the project explores the meaning of quality of life, dignity-enhancing assistive devices, and the importance of communities and one’s home - especially for the elderly. These perspectives also include the significance of place-specific design and the rationale for transformations, as well as how operational and embedded energy are balanced in today’s architecture. Læsø and the site are examined through various analyses, while a synopsis and selected case studies summarise and provide inspiration for a longer design process across scales, topics, and areas of the site.

The result is an environmentally and socially sustainable, place-specific design that explores the benefits and possibilities of transforming existing buildings at a specific location on Læsø to dignifying transitional housing for senior and elderly, increasing the quality of life for older citizens.

projects.title: Remain
projects.abstract:
This thesis investigates how circular economy principles can be translated into a viable product design within the contract furniture market. The project aimed to extend product lifetimes and reduce throw-away culture while maintaining a feasible business case in a highly competitive and saturated industry. Through research, user interviews, market analysis, and expert input, key challenges related to product longevity, repairability, and access to environmental data for ESG reporting were identified.

As a result, Remain was developed as a modular and repairable conference chair for conference, event, and hotel settings, with Comwell serving as the primary case study throughout the project. The design focuses on modularity, lightweight construction, repairability, easiness of use and improved end-of-life handling in order to reduce environmental impact and companies total cost of ownership. In addition, the concept integrates accessible product-specific sustainability data through an ESG nutrition label to support companies’ increasing ESG reporting needs.

The collaboration with HAY further strengthened the project’s feasibility by aligning the proposal with existing production capabilities and opportunities for scalable implementation. The project ultimately translates the intention of extending product lifetimes into a feasible and scalable product proposal for the saturated and highly competitive “red ocean” contract furniture market.

projects.title: PrySafe
Making Death Manageable: A Sociological Study of Crematorium Work
projects.abstract:
This thesis examines how Danish crematory workers develop and apply professional, emotional, and symbolic strategies in their work with death, and how they experience public reactions to and perceptions of their profession. The thesis seeks to contribute to a sociological understanding of how death work is managed, experienced, and assigned meaning within a contemporary Danish context.

The study is inspired by Derek Layder’s adaptive approach and combines qualitative interviews and fieldwork conducted at six Danish crematories. The analytical framework is informed by symbolic interactionism and draws on orienting concepts related to death work, interaction, emotional labor, and stigma. Through a continuous dialogue between theory and empirical material, the thesis explores how crematory workers navigate the practical, emotional, and social dimensions of working closely with the dead.

The analysis demonstrates that crematory work involves far more than the technical handling of dead bodies. Crematory workers continuously regulate proximity and distance to death through routines, language, humour, emotional regulation, and interactional practices. The study further shows how the dead body shifts between different symbolic positions throughout the cremation process, moving between understandings of personhood, materiality, and the professional work objects. Emotional distance therefore emerges not as emotional detachment, but as a necessary and ongoing regulation that enables workers to remain in close contact with death without becoming overwhelmed by it.

At the same time, crematory workers encounter fascination, discomfort, silence, and moral suspicion in public understandings of their profession. In response, they develop different forms of stigma management and actively construct professional meaning, legitimacy, and pride around their work. The thesis thus argues that crematory work should be understood not simply as a technical form of labor, but as a complex form of death work involving the continuous negotiation of death’s emotional, symbolic, and social significance in contemporary society.

Keywords: adaptive theory; orienting concepts; symbolic interactionism; death work; crematory workers; cremation; dramaturgy; emotional labor; stigma; stigma management; dirty work; fieldwork; qualitative interviews; sociology of death work; emotional regulation

projects.title: INTACT: Off-Grid Energy Architectures for Emergency Shelter Operation at CEMTEC
Streetscapes
projects.abstract: This thesis seeks to explore a visionary and participatory approach to transforming urban mobilities and streets within inner cities, using Aalborg as a design case. This is done though an integrated design process, using a theoretical foundation based on theories from the mobilities turn, social futures and notions of justice as well as case studies of four cities, that investigate measures needed to create inclusive and context-sensitive design. The main argument is that challenging the dominance of cars in urban streets starts with a social imagination of streets without cars, and that to do so, we must challenge how we perceive urban streets and their users and change the design process for transforming urban streets. The design proposal consists of a vision and mobility strategy for Aalborg and transformations of three streets. The thesis shows that moving towards sustainable urban mobilities requires a change of mindset, process and solutions and that motivations for using the street can be used as an operational tool in co-transformation of urban streets.

How are the informal caregivers burdened? A mixed methods thesis in sociology
projects.abstract:
In light of the demographic changes, shortages of labour within the welfare sector, and a growing reliance on home-based care, increasing responsibility for care is being assigned to
informal caregivers. Existing research shows that informal caregivers often play a crucial role in supporting the one in need, but also that caregiving may negatively affect caregivers’ own
wellbeing. However, much existing research approaches informal caregivers as a resource to
be exploited, rather than as individuals in their own right. This thesis examines how caregiver
burden may be expressed and how informal caregivers themselves experience and interpret the burden.
The thesis applies a mixed methods design combining quantitative and qualitative approaches. First, a quantitative analysis based on cross-sectional survey data from the Danish
health survey Hvordan har du det? (2025) is conducted to identify the characteristics associated
with particularly burdened caregivers and the patterns in caregiver burden. Secondly, these findings are utilized in regard to the qualitative approach for recruitment strategies and used in
the semi-structures interviews with eleven female informal caregivers aged 25-54 with children
living at home. The thesis places particular emphasis on the findings from the qualitative data.
Drawing on the theoretical perspectives of Joan Tronto and Arlie Russel Hochschild, the analysis focuses particularly on care work, emotion management, and the structural and
emotional dimensions of caregiver burden.
This thesis finds that informal caregivers experience extensive burden through the multiple “caps” they carry, where they continuously navigate multiple roles and responsibilities simultaneously. The findings show that caregivers may move between several phases of care at the same time, which can contribute to mental, social, physical, financial and emotional burden. Furthermore, the findings indicate that informal caregivers are a suitable subject for
identifying extensive emotion management, as they appear highly aware and reflective of both
the rules and benefits of managing their emotions. The thesis also contributes to the theoretical field by extending Joan Tronto’s phases of care with a sixth phase, termed ‘caring for self’,
along the ethical element ‘self-awareness’, which highlights the impact that care work may
have on the caregiver’s own wellbeing.

New advances in Light Alkanes Oxidation using N2O over Metal-Organic Framework Catalysts for Power-to-X Fuel Production
projects.abstract: The catalytic oxidation of light alkanes into alcohols over metal organic frameworks (MOFs) represents a promising route for sustainable e-fuel production. However, achieving sufficient conversion and selectivity under mild conditions remains a major challenge. This study investigates the catalytic oxidation of propane to propanol over MIL-100(Fe) as a model system, with the aim of improving reaction performance and gaining insight into key operating parameters. Experiments were conducted in a packed bed reactor under varying catalyst loading, reactant ratios, and flow conditions, with particular focus on the effect of space velocity. The results show that space velocity plays a critical role in controlling both conversion and selectivity. Lower space velocities increase conversion but promote over-oxidation, whereas higher space velocities improve selectivity at the expense of conversion. In addition, variations in space velocity were found to significantly influence the kinetic behavior of the reaction: increasing catalyst loading and reactant concentration enhanced conversion of N2O, while increasing the flow rate reduced it conversion. These effects impact the overall reaction performance. All these findings provide valuable insight into the optimization of alkane oxidation and contribute to the development of more efficient processes for sustainable fuel production within Power-to-X applications.

projects.title: Community x100
projects.abstract:
This project explores everyday life and community dynamics in the village of Stjær, with a focus on inclusion and user-centered design. The aim is to understand how to bring more life to the old village centre through participatory design.

The study is based on an interactive design process combining background research, site visits, interviews, and mapping. Walking interviews and workshops with residents provided insight into local experiences and needs.

The findings highlight the importance of community engagement, volunteer activities, and the maintenance of social life in the village. They also reveal challenges with accessibility to common institutions, as well as question the role of the urban designer in a very independent community.

The project proposes design strategies that support inclusive, community-driven development and strengthen everyday social interaction in rural contexts.

projects.title: FELT
projects.abstract:
Professionals working with livestock operate in physically demanding, unpredictable, and hygiene-sensitive environments, where equipment must be accessed and handled while working close to large animals. Farm veterinarians and farmers often rely on improvised solutions such as placing equipment boxes on the ground, carrying equipment and medicine in pockets, or walking repeatedly between animals, equipment, and vehicles. These practices create inefficiencies in the workflow, increase physical strain, reduce overview, and contribute to unsafe needle handling.
This project addresses the need for a workflow-oriented equipment system that supports accessibility, ergonomics, organization, hygiene, and safer handling of equipment during animal treatment. Developed in collaboration with farm veterinarians at Vendsyssel Landdyrlæger and BoviCura, the project was carried out through a co-evolutionary and design thinking process, combining field visits, observations, interviews, reference studies, bodystorming, mockups, prototype testing, user feedback, and technical detailing.
FELT is a workflow-oriented equipment box system, designed to bring equipment closer to the point of use. The system consists of a hanging platform, interchangeable FELT Boxes for organization, and recessed placements for approved sharps containers. By positioning equipment at an ergonomic working height near the animals, FELT reduces the need for bending down, repeated movement, and temporary storage of needles in pockets or on ground surfaces.
FELT includes small and medium variants for different equipment needs, while the large variant remains a future development opportunity. Overall, the project demonstrates how workflow insights can be translated into a practical, scalable, and production-oriented product system for professionals working with and treating animals.

projects.title: Development of Fixed Frequency High Efficiency Flyback Converter for Satellite Power Supply
projects.abstract: In the modern world, satellites have become essential for both civil, scientific and industrial purposes. Due to simplicity and reliability, it is decided to investigate variants of flyback converter topologies to increase efficiency compared to the conventional flyback. The bidirectional flyback converter is chosen, due to its ability to achieve soft-switching reducing switching losses, and large peak currents is identified as a problem, which must be solved to achieve the benefits of this topology. The turns ratio is found so as to minimise the combined RMS-current of all the windings. However, this necessitates a large air gap which results in large leakage inductances. Using the extended cantilever model, the effective turns ratio and leakage inductances are identified, and converter clamps and snubbers are designed to absorb the large energy stored in leakage inductances. Compared to theoretical data of a conventional flyback converter, the prototype developed in this project shows low efficiency of 60-70\%. In order to improve this, the leakage inductance of the transformer should be reduced to lower the losses generated in snubbers and clamps. These improvements would have to be made, before it can be determined, whether the bidirectional flyback converter is suitable as a replacement for the conventional flyback converter.

projects.title: Control of a Wind Turbine
"You didn't realize that you didn't know": Design toolkit for Unknown Unknown discovery in chatbots
projects.abstract: The paper explores how chatbot interaction design can support the discovery of “unknown unknowns”. We present a design toolkit for conversational and pre-conversational discovery strategies in Large Language Model (LLM)-based healthcare chatbots. We examine the use case of supporting newly discharged stroke survivors through two user studies with stroke survivors, stroke clinicians, and university students. Study 1 investigated four pre-conversational interface paradigms for navigating stroke-related information: Categories, FAQ, Roles, and Keywords. Results showed strong preference for structured category-based navigation and layout, while highlighting the importance of accessibility considerations. Building on these findings, Study 2 examined how users discover new information through faceted and conversational interaction. A chatbot prototype supporting faceted and conversational search was evaluated across different scenario types and suggestion button strategies. Results indicate that vague scenarios encouraged greater use of predefined prompts, supporting exploratory discovery of unknown topics, while specific scenarios led users towards custom questions. Participants generally perceived the system as intuitive and supportive, though limitations still need to be addressed for future works. The paper contributes both a design toolkit and insights from two studies into discovery-oriented chatbot interaction design.

projects.title: NEO Rollator - Breaking The Stigma Of Mobility Aids
projects.abstract:
The purpose of this Master’s thesis project is to describe the industrial
design engineering process behind NEO: a next-generation rollator
optimised to break the psychological stigma barriers that delay mobility
adoption among active older adults.
Utilising a user-centred design approach, the process integrates
qualitative field data gathered by visiting local activity centres, conducting
comprehensive interviews with current users, and engaging with pre-users
to map their insights, fears, and aesthetic opinions. Additionally, technical
manufacturing capabilities are explored directly in collaboration with
Wolturnus.
The final design demonstrates how an empowering, lifestyle-focused
product language can break the adoption paradox, making preventative
mobility support both dignified and engaging for the ordinary senior.

projects.title: The Evi Crib
projects.abstract:
This report investigates how the hospital crib can better support bonding, postpartum recovery, and a more homelike maternity environment. Existing cribs were identified as highly clinical solutions that create distance between parents and baby while limiting maternal autonomy after birth. The project resulted in Evi, a parent-centred hospital crib designed to improve closeness, accessibility, and recovery through bedside positioning, sliding nests and ergonomic height adjustment

The design follows relevant medical standards and is bedwasher compatible, while combining clinical functionality with emotional wellbeing and parental equality. The project also reflects on the challenges of balancing safety, hygiene, usability, and aesthetics within a highly regulated healthcare context.

Social Norms and Diffusion Processes in Adolescents Puff Bar Use: A Contribution to Primary Prevention in a Municipal Context
projects.abstract:
Title: Social Norms and Diffusion Processes in Adolescents Puff Bar Use: A Contribution to
Primary Prevention in a Municipal Context.
Background: Puff bar use among adolescents is increasing and represents a public health
challenge. The products are easily accessible, available in attractive flavours, and often circu-
late through social networks. This suggests that use is shaped by norms, relationships, and ex-
posure in young people’s everyday environments.
Aim: To examine how social norms and diffusion processes related to puff bar use among
lower secondary school students can be understood, and how this knowledge can be used to
qualify the development of a primary preventive intervention in Frederikshavn Municipality.
Method: The thesis is based on the Medical Research Council’s (MRC) framework for de-
veloping complex interventions. It combines a systematic literature review, a questionnaire
survey among lower secondary school students in Frederikshavn Municipality, and qualita-
tive interviews with adolescents. The analysis is grounded in a hermeneutic approach.
Results: Puff bar use among young people is closely connected to social relationships,
norms, and exposure. Students who have seen people in their network use puff bars has sig-
nificantly higher odds of using the product themselves (OR = 11.100; CI: 1.505-81.927). The
qualitative analysis shows that puff bars are often introduced early through friends and over
time their use may shift from social experimentation to a way of managing stress and discom-
fort. The literature also indicates that interactive and norm-correcting interventions focusing
on coping and action competence can influence young people’s attitudes and intentions re-
garding use.
Conclusion: Adolescent’s use of puff bars should be understood as a socially embedded
practice shaped by visibility, accessibility, communities, and norms. Municipal primary pre-
vention should therefore be initiated early in the diffusion process, before use becomes an es-
tablished part of youth communities. The revised program theory suggests that social norms
approaches, and norm correction are relevant elements, but that prevention should also ad-
dress the social meanings that link puff bars to status, belonging, and identity. A preventive
intervention should therefore be multifaceted, interactive, school-based, and locally embed-
ded in municipal practice.

Lodret liv - Transformation of Aalborg University Hospital North
projects.abstract:
Vestbyen is a dense and diverse neighborhood with a strong local identity and community life. The area has a growing need for larger housing, shared spaces, cultural activities, and places where different generations can meet. Located at the entrance to Vestbyen, Buildings B and P at Aalborg University Hospital have the potential to become an active part of the neighborhood and strengthen the existing community and character of Vestbyen.
This thesis explores how the existing hospital buildings can be transformed to respond to the social and spatial needs of Vestbyen through new functions, spatial changes, and architectural interventions. The project proposes a mixed-use vertical community containing housing, workplaces, cultural functions, public spaces, and shared facilities connected through open and interconnected spaces. Through analysis, sketching, technical studies, and design development, the project investigates how the existing modernist structure can be reused and adapted to create stronger connections between the buildings and the surrounding city. The final proposal aims to create a more active, inclusive, and socially connected environment while supporting the identity, everyday life, and existing community of Vestbyen.

projects.title: The Kilogram and the Prayer: Suffering, Meaning, and Care Among Survivors of the July 2024 Movement in Bangladesh
projects.abstract: This thesis examines how five male survivors of the July 2024 political movement in Bangladesh make sense of post-violence suffering, and where their conceptualisations resonate with, or exceed, the mental health and psychosocial frameworks available to them. Drawing on in-depth interviews conducted in collaboration with the Human Rights Development Centre (HRDC) and DIGNITY – Danish Institute Against Torture, and analysed through constructivist grounded theory, the study traces eight inductive themes and develops two conceptual arguments. The first, theological distress constitution, names a pattern in which religious framing functions not as a channel through which a prior distress is communicated but as the register within which distress is produced, measured, and given moral weight. The second, functional-material distress, names a pattern in which suffering is conceptualised through the precise daily transactions of reduced capability rather than through affective categories. The thesis argues that these two registers are not parallel but constitutively intersecting — most visibly in one participant's account of his violence reaching into the practice of prayer through which his relationship with God is maintained. The contribution is offered as an analytical proposal grounded in five specific accounts, with disproportionate weight resting on one extraordinary informant, and as an invitation to further empirical investigation in similar post-violence contexts.

projects.title: Does the Boston Naming Test Work in a Sample of Young Adults? An Examination of the Construct Validity of the Boston Naming Test in a Sample of Young Adult Danes.
projects.abstract:
The following thesis is written as a collaboration between the Neurological Department of Aalborg University’s Hospital and myself. It sets out to examine the construct validity of the Boston Naming Test (BNT) in a sample of young adults aged 18-39 and additionally aims to identify problematic items which could threaten its construct validity. Through the use of language data obtained from Korpus.dsl.dk it is established that several of the items in the BNT have become very infrequent, potentially to the point of becoming too difficult. Thus, it is established that a re-examination of the test in a Danish context is due. To examine this, the thesis draws upon several streams of empirical data and theory. Chiefly, the thesis draws upon the Latent Variable Theory of measurement to make inferences and to guide its analysis. Additionally, relevant theory pertaining to picture naming as well as auxiliary theory on topics such as semantic memory and visual perception has been included to nuance the discussion and analysis. Data was collected through a non-experimental empirical design, where 70 participants were recruited for testing on the full 60-item version of the BNT. Rasch analysis was used to investigate the data. The statistical analysis found that the BNT was not meaningfully able to differentiate between the vast majority of participants in this sample, as its items were for the most part too easy to do this. Interestingly, four specific items were identified as potentially problematic, these being “knocker”, “latch”, “yoke” and “trellis”. “Knocker”, “yoke” and “trellis” were all identified as being potentially problematic due to their difficulty. Over 90% of participants failed to correctly name either “yoke” or “trellis” and 60,9% failed to name “knocker”. Thus, while the test was generally found to be easy, there were also items which were extremely difficult for my sample. “Latch” was found to have an inverse item-total correlation of -.247, indicating that the better one performs on the BNT in general, the lower the odds were of correctly identifying the item. An additional finding was that the sample in this thesis achieved a mean total score of 52,7 (SD = 3), which is significantly lower than Danish norms as estimated using a single sample T-test. It should however be noted that it is debateable to what degree these findings can be generalized, due to several limitations. These include the fact that the sample is only made up of healthy young adults, the participant’s educational background and the fact that only one group was included in the study, making direct comparisons between groups impossible.
Overall, the study finds that it is questionable whether the construct validity of the BNT can be considered adequate in a sample of young Danish adults. Additionally, four items have been identified which could potentially be changed for more modern items in order to improve the construct validity of the BNT.

projects.title: Effect of Real Weld Geometry on Multiaxial Fatigue Predictions Using 3D Scanned Welds
projects.abstract:
Scatter in predicted fatigue life of welded
joints is large since idealised design notches
do not represent actual geometric varia-
tions at the weld toe. This project inves-
tigates whether high-fidelity 3D scans of
as-built weld geometries can improve fa-
tigue life prediction for axially and torsion-
ally loaded tube-to-tube joints. Nineteen
specimens were scanned, converted to CAD
and analysed using submodel-based FEA.
Fatigue tests in the lab were performed
in parallel. Local stress concentration
factors and multiaxial stress components
at the weld toe were extracted, and the
Gough–Pollard criterion was applied with
these stresses and reference base-material
S–N curves. Results show that the scat-
ter was the same for both approaches when
considerin nominal stress. When re-plotted
in terms of a local Gough–Pollard equiv-
alent stress, both prediction sets collapse
tightly onto their own S–N curves, with the
3D scans giving the lowest standard devia-
tion in log-life. The remaining scatter rela-
tive to experiment is attributed to internal
flaws and other imperfections not captured
by surface scans.

projects.title: Therapists' Experiences in Therapy with Patients with Pathological Narcissism
projects.abstract:
This thesis investigates how therapists experience working with patients with patholog-
ical narcissism through a phenomenological lens. The thesis consists of an empirical article
(Part A) and an extended exploration of the theoretical and methodological foundations of the
study (Part B).
Theoretically, the thesis draws on contemporary understandings of pathological narcis-
sism as a relational and affective disturbance characterized by dysregulated self-esteem, affect
regulation, and interpersonal functioning. Furthermore, phenomenology, as well as phenome-
nological psychopathology, are integrated, with a particular focus on the dimensions of lived
time, body, space, and relation as fundamental structures of human being-in-the-world.
Empirically, the study is based on semi-structured interviews with seven therapists, who
together described experiences from therapeutic work with 23 patients with pathological nar-
cissism. The material was analyzed through an iterative, phenomenologically inspired analytic
process focusing on the therapists’ lived experiences.
The findings show that therapeutic work with patients with pathological narcissism is
often experienced as emotionally intense and destabilizing. Therapists’ experiences of lived
time, body, space, and relation are continuously altered and challenged in encounters with these
patients. Time is experienced as circular, stagnant, stretched, without future, or intensified; the
body as distant or erased, overactivated and requiring regulation, and caught between fusion
and separation; space as asymmetrically organized, shifting between distance and closeness,
openness and constriction, and at times experienced as unstable or threatening; and the thera-
peutic relation as asymmetrical and hierarchically organized, non-reciprocal and instrumental,
marked by struggles over position, devaluation and instability, yet at times receding into the
background as implicit and unproblematic. The analysis further suggests that different narcis-
sistic manifestations are associated with distinct ways of experiencing the therapeutic situa-
tion.
The thesis thus contributes to a phenomenological understanding of how pathological
narcissism not only shapes the patient’s way of being in the world, but also the therapist’s way
of being-in-the-situation. Furthermore, the thesis highlights the clinical implications of under-
standing therapists’ experiences as meaningful and situated rather than merely expressions of
individual shortcomings or professional inadequacies, and suggests that the dimensions of lived
time, body, space, and relation may function as reflective orientation points in therapeutic
work.

Between Requirements and Practice. Local Government Manager's Handling of IT Security
projects.abstract:
This thesis examines how managers working at Viborg Kommune work to uphold the core task amid increasing demands for IT-security and compliance. The study is based on a qualitative single-case study of Viborg Kommune and draws on semi-structured interviews with managers from both the employment sector and the IT-department. The background for the study is the growing digitalization of the public sector, a shifting landscape regarding cyber-threats, and increasing regulatory requirements for IT-security, including the NIS 2-directive. These developments have contributed to making IT-security an increasingly integrated part of the local governments management tasks. The thesis findings are based on three organizational levels: strategic, middle-management and institutional.

The thesis therefore investigates how managers perceive, interpret, and handle IT-security requirements in practice, and how these requirements influence their managerial room for manoeuvre. The analysis is grounded in Street-level Management and Situational Work, which are used to illuminate the managers’ organisational priorities, assessments, and handling of conflict in demands regarding the organisational practice. The findings indicate that managers must continuously balance considerations related to security, operations, development, and citizen interaction. At the same time, the analysis shows that IT-security is no longer perceived solely as a technical domain but as an organizational and managerial responsibility that shapes everyday work practices.

Furthermore, the findings suggest that IT-security work generates new forms of organizational coordination and interdependence between managers, IT-specialists and other organizational functions. Simultaneously, the increased security requirements may challenge flexibility, accessibility and efficient operations within the local government. The thesis contributes a practice-oriented understanding of how managers working at Viborg Kommune handles IT-security in an organizational context characterized by digitalization, heightened security demand and a complex threat-landscape. In doing so, it adds to research on public management, digitalization and the organizational implications of IT-security in the public sector.
The findings can be transferred to other danish local governments due the thesis’ most-likely case design. It can therefore be assumed that they (other participants in DBS) share the same experiences as Viborg Kommune.

Leaving Children's and Family Services: Organisation, Professional Practice and Meaning in Social Work
projects.abstract:
Abstract
This thesis examines how organisational conditions shape social workers’ opportunities to exercise professional judgment, experience meaning in their work, and remain in the field of child and family services. The study begins in a broader welfare context marked by increasing administrative demands, standardisation, and growing concerns about moral stress, burnout, and employee turnover among social workers. Against this backdrop, the thesis investigates MIFU on Bornholm as a case of organisational “positive deviance” within social work practice.
Empirically, the thesis is based on ethnographic fieldwork in MIFU, including participant observations, naturally occurring data, informal interviews, and document analysis. Analytically, the study draws on perspectives from Street-Level Bureaucracy theory, combined with Self-Determination Theory, as a framework for understanding how organisational conditions shape social workers’ well-being and experience of meaning at work.
The analysis is structured around seven organisational microchanges identified through the empirical material. These microchanges include organising work around the young person’s needs, professional autonomy in frontline practice, working in partnerships, organised professional communities, relational forms of documentation, mobile work practices, and the physical environment. Rather than presenting MIFU as an ideal model, the thesis examines how concrete organisational arrangements create different conditions for professional practice, relational work, and meaningful experiences.
The analysis shows how organising work around the young person’s needs and placing decision-making authority closer to frontline practitioners, expands social workers’ opportunities to act on professional judgments and engage in more flexible and relational forms of practice. At the same time, partnerships and collective professional structures appear to function as organisational ‘protective mechanisms’, distributing responsibility, emotional strain, and complex decision-making across the team. Furthermore, the study demonstrates how documentation, mobility, and physical space can become integrated parts of relational social work rather than merely administrative or logistical conditions surrounding it.
However, the thesis also highlights important tensions within these organisational forms. Increased flexibility and autonomy may intensify the emotional demands of the work and blur boundaries between professional and private life. Likewise, relational forms of practice may come into tension with bureaucratic demands for documentation, standardisation, and measurable outcomes. The analysis therefore argues that organisational microchanges do not eliminate dilemmas in social work, but rather shift and reshape them.
Overall, the thesis contributes with a practice-oriented perspective on how relatively ‘small’ organisational changes may create significantly different conditions for relational and meaningful social work without requiring large-scale structural reforms. The study thus points to organisation itself as a central condition for professional well-being and the possibility of practicing relational welfare work.

projects.title: Burnout and Self-Compassion Among Psychologists Working in Regional Psychiatry - A Mixed Methods Study
Pyrus Gate - When Citizens and Archives Do Not Speak the Same Language
projects.abstract:
This thesis investigates how young citizens aged 18-30 perceive archives and their societal role, and which opportunities and barriers these perceptions create in relation to archival communication and user engagement. The study is based on four qualitative semi-structured interviews with young citizens from Aalborg Municipality, and draws on a phenomenological approach focused on lived experiences and everyday understandings.
The analysis demonstrates that the participants primarily associate archives with physical storage, old documents, dust and historical preservation, often shaped by popular culture rather than personal experience. At the same time, their own information practices are characterized by digital accessibility, immediacy and intuitive search systems. Drawing on theories of social acceleration, this thesis argues that a temporal and linguistic gap exists between the institutional logic of archives and the participants’ everyday life-worlds.
Furthermore, this thesis shows that archives are often perceived as culturally and institutionally distant, creating uncertainty about how archives are used in practice. The study argues that archival accessibility is therefore not solely a question of digitization for example, but also of translation, intuitiveness, and institutional visibility.
Ultimately, this thesis highlights the importance of understanding non-users, if archives wish to remain relevant public and democratic institutions in contemporary society.

projects.title: "We Mostly Stay Together" - social participation among children with disabilities in education outside the classroom
projects.abstract:
Dette speciale undersøger social deltagelse blandt børn med funktionsnedsættelser i udeskole på en dansk specialskole. Børn med funktionsnedsættelser har en øget risiko for begrænset deltagelse i skolens sociale og faglige fællesskaber, hvilket kan påvirke deres trivsel, læring og oplevelse af tilhørsforhold. Udeskole er en læringsmetode, som er blevet udbredt i danske specialskoler, hvor 56,6% rapporterer, at de praktiserer udeskole regelmæssigt. Udeskole inden for almenområdet har vist sig at kunne fremme elevers læringsprocesser gennem praktiske, kropslige og sanselige erfaringer, der kan styrke læring, trivsel og sundhed. Samtidig findes der begrænset viden om, hvordan børn med funktionsnedsættelser selv oplever deltagelse i denne kontekst, samt hvordan deltagelse produceres, udfordres og understøttes i hverdagsinteraktioner. Specialet bidrager til dette felt ved at analysere deltagelse som et relationelt og situeret fænomen, der konstant formes i samspillet mellem børn, voksne og omgivelserne.

Formålet er at undersøge, hvordan børn med funktionsnedsættelser oplever og forhandler social deltagelse i udeskole, og under hvilke betingelser deltagelse muliggøres eller begrænses. Undersøgelsen er gennemført som et kvalitativt casestudie af én dansk specialskole med lang erfaring med udeskole. Feltarbejde blev gennemført over otte skoledage i marts 2026. Det empiriske materiale er indsamlet gennem deltagerobservationer samt interviews med udvalgte elever på tværs af tre klassetrin med henblik på at få indblik i børns egne erfaringer med udeskole.

Undersøgelsen bygger på kritisk realisme, hvor sociale fænomener forstås som relationelle og lagdelte, og hvor analysen bevæger sig fra empiriske observationer mod underliggende mekanismer. På denne baggrund anvendes en abduktiv analysestrategi, hvor det empiriske materiale fortolkes i samspil med teoretiske begreber. Som overordnet analytisk orientering inddrages Disabled Children’s Childhood Studies (DCCS), der betoner børn med funktionsnedsættelser som aktive deltagere i sociale praksisser. Det teoretiske begrebsapparat kombinerer Maciver et al.’s deltagelsesmodel med mikrosociale interaktionsteorier. Maciver et al. anvendes til at strukturere analysen på tværs af kontekster og til at skelne mellem forskellige former for deltagelse. Til at analysere hvordan deltagelse produceres i konkrete situationer, anvendes Erving Goffmans begreber om roller, face-work og misinvolvering, der belyser børns forhandling af sociale positioner i interaktioner. Samtidig anvendes Randall Collins’ teori om interaktionsritualer til at undersøge, hvordan deltagelse opretholdes eller bryder sammen gennem fælles fokus, emotionel energi og gruppesolidaritet.

Analysen viser, at social deltagelse i klasselokalet er en relationel proces, som i høj grad afhænger af forudsigelige strukturer, tydelige roller og løbende voksenmediering. Når disse betingelser udfordres, kan deltagelsen destabiliseres og føre til tilbagetrækning og konflikt. Denne kontekst danner en vigtig baggrund for at forstå de alternative deltagelsesformer, som udeskole muliggør. I udeskole fremstår deltagelse som en praksis, hvor deltagelsesformer i højere grad kan udfolde sig fleksibelt. Her organiseres aktiviteter omkring fælles opgaver som madlavning over bål, bevægelse og ophold i naturen, hvilket skaber situationer med delt fokus og mulighed for varieret engagement. Analysen viser, at børn i højere grad kan deltage på forskellige måder, gennem aktiv deltagelse, observation eller midlertidig tilbagetrækning, uden at miste deres tilknytning til fællesskabet. Særligt fremhæves det, at perifer deltagelse, hvor børn er til stede uden aktivt at deltage i fælles aktiviteter, kan udgøre en legitim og socialt accepteret form for deltagelse. Samtidig viser analysen, at udeskole ikke automatisk skaber inklusion. Der opstår fortsat situationer med eksklusion, hvor deltagelse bryder sammen. Disse situationer håndteres forskelligt afhængigt af timing og tilgængelighed af mediering fra voksne og jævnaldrende, samt de organisatoriske betingelser der omgiver dem. På tværs af analysen identificeres en række betingelser, der muliggør deltagelse. Disse omfatter blandt andet fleksibel organisering, adgang til forskellige roller, tolerance for variation i engagement samt sociale relationer præget af omsorg og gensidig støtte. Omvendt begrænses deltagelse i situationer, hvor strukturer er rigide, hvor muligheder for alternative deltagelsesformer er begrænsede, eller hvor sociale processer som grænsedragning ikke adresseres.

På tværs af analyserne fremstår social deltagelse ikke som en individuel egenskab hos barnet, men som en relationel og situeret proces, der kontinuerligt bliver forhandlet i samspillet mellem organisatoriske rammer, sociale relationer og konkrete aktiviteter. Udeskole fremstår som en praksis, der kan skabe særligt gunstige betingelser for mere fleksible former for deltagelse, men som samtidig kræver opmærksomhed på de sociale mekanismer, der både kan muliggøre og begrænse børns muligheder for deltagelse i fællesskaber. Resultaterne peger på, at inklusion i højere grad bør forstås som et spørgsmål om organisering og relationelle betingelser snarere end om individets ressourcer. Dermed peger specialets resultater på implikationer for både pædagogisk praksis og socialt arbejde, hvor fokus med fordel kan rettes mod, hvordan deltagelse understøttes i praksis.

projects.title: More than an artist daughter - A polyphonic biographic analysis of Helga Ancher
projects.abstract: This thesis examines how a polyphonic biographical approach can contribute to a more nuanced understanding of Helga Ancher. Although Helga was a renowned artist herself, the existing literature primarily defines her as the shy and secluded daughter of the more celebrated Skagen painters, Anna and Michael Ancher. Drawing on Birgitte Possing’s biographical archetypes, the thesis uses a polyphonic approach that integrates multiple voices and source types to create a fragmented portrait. Using letters from acquaintances, material artefacts and visual sources, the thematic analysis demonstrates how Helga emerges as a more complex figure, who was very intellectual, congenial, emotionally multifaceted, and artistically independent. The thesis highlights how letters both reproduce and challenge the existing narratives, while visual and material sources give insight into Helga’s self-perception. The diverse source material has resulted in competing interpretations that coexist rather than resolve into a singular, defined narrative. While the polyphonic approach enables a distinct and less reductive biography, the thesis also addresses its methodological limitations, including dissonance and dependence on extensive source material. Ultimately, the study argues that a polyphonic approach not only nuances the portrayal of Helga but also emphasizes the interpretative nature of biographical writing itself.

projects.title: A Qualitative study of Honour-Related Social Control and Social Work in RED safehouse
Leaving a Home Without a Place to Land
projects.abstract:
This thesis examines the significance of housing and social networks for women exposed to intimate partner violence in the Faroe Islands and their possibilities for leaving violent relationships and establishing an independent life afterwards. The study is situated within a Faroese context characterized by housing shortages, rising housing prices, and small, closely connected communities, which may influence women’s opportunities and access to support after leaving domestic violence. Particular attention is directed toward the period following shelter stay or counselling at Kvinnuhúsið, the Faroe Islands’ only specialized violence support and shelter organization.

This thesis is based on a hermeneutic and abductive research approach and combines qualitative interviews with formerly abused women, violence counsellors, and a politicial with quantitative data and document analysis.

The analytical framework draws on Pierre Bourdieu’s concepts of capital, habitus, and field, alongside an intersectional perspective and claimsmaking theory. While the intersectional perspective is applied to examine how overlapping social positions shape women’s vulnerability, claimsmaking theory is used to analyse how housing problems and the need for longer-term support are articulated and recognized within practice and political contexts.

The findings indicate that leaving an abusive relationship cannot be understood as a single individual decision, but rather as a complex and often long-term process shaped by social and structural conditions. Limitied access to affordable and stable housing may discourage women from leaving violent relationships, prolong stays at shelters, or contribute to women returning to abusive partners. Housing therefore appears not merely as a practical issue, but as a structural condition connected to safety, recovery, empowerment, and the possibility of creating an independent life free from violence.

The analysis further demonstrates that social networks play an ambivalent role. In the Faroese small context, networks may provide crucial access to housing, emotional support, and practical assistance. At the same time, the empirical findings suggest that social networks are not always experienced as available or safe to rely on. The women describe feelings of concerns about burdening others, which may limit their willingness to seek help.

Particular vulnerability is identified among foreign women living in the Faroe Islands. The analysis show how insecure residence status, limited knowledge of the Faroese welfare system and economic dependency may reinforce one another and intensify women’s vulnerability during the separation process. Through an intersectional perspective, the thesis demonstrates how gender, migration status, housing conditions, economic dependency and living on a isolated island intersect and shape women’s opportunities for leaving violence and rebuilding their lives.

This thesis also highlights how the issue of housing for women leaving violent relationships has become recognized and articulated within both practice and political contexts. Through a claimsmaking perspective, Kvinnuhúsið emerges as a central actor in drawing attention to the need for longer-term support and housing solutions for women. However, the findings suggest that although the problem is acknowledged politically, this recognition has not been translated into concrete and institutionalized long-term housing initiatives.

Overall, the thesis concludes that women’s opportunities to establish a life free from violence in the Faroe Islands are closely connected to broader social and structural conditions. Access to stable housing, financial resources, social support, and institutional assistance appears essential in enabling women to maintain separation from violence and create sustainable and independent lives. Violence in intimate relationships must therefore be understood not only as an individual or private issue, but also as a structural and societal concern shaped by broader social and housing conditions within Faroese society.

Seasonal and Spatial Variation in Lake Macroinvertebrate Assemblages and Their Influence on DLMI Scoring
projects.abstract:
Seasonal variation in macroinvertebrate communities may influence ecological assessment results
in lakes and therefore affect the interpretation of ecological status under the European
Union Water Framework Directive (WFD). In Denmark, ecological assessment of lake littoral
macroinvertebrates is conducted using the Danish Littoral Macroinvertebrate Index (DLMI),
which is typically based on autumn sampling. However, the extent to which seasonal variation
affects DLMI values and macroinvertebrate community composition has not previously been
systematically investigated.
This study examined seasonal variation in littoral macroinvertebrate communities across five
Danish lakes. Macroinvertebrate samples were collected during spring, summer, and autumn
of 2025. Ecological status was assessed using DLMI, while seasonal and spatial variation
in community composition were analyzed using non-metric multidimensional scaling (NMDS),
permutational multivariate analysis of variance (PERMANOVA), indicator species analysis, and
beta diversity.
The results showed that DLMI values and ecological status classes were generally stable
across seasons, indicating limited seasonal influence on ecological classification. Differences
among lakes were substantially stronger than seasonal differences, suggesting that local
environmental conditions and lake typology play a larger role in the the structuring of
macroinvertebrate assemblages than short-term seasonal variation. NMDS and PERMANOVA
analyses demonstrated significant seasonal variation in community composition, although the
effect of lake identity explained a larger proportion of the observed variation. Beta diversity
analyses further indicated that differences among communities were primarily driven by species
turnover rather than nestedness.
Overall, the findings suggest that DLMI is relatively robust to seasonal variation in the
investigated lakes and support the continued use of autumn sampling in Danish lake monitoring.
However, variationincommunitycompositionindicatesthatecologicalpatternsmaydifferamong
seasons and lake types.

Minimizing Parasitic forces in Ironcore Linear motors
projects.abstract: This project investigates the presence and mitigation of parasitic forces and torques in an iron-core Linear Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (LPMSM). These effects can negatively affect positioning accuracy, standstill stability, and overall motion performance in high-precision applications. To study these phenomena, an experimental test platform was developed consisting of a linear motor, a custom control system, and a multi-axis force/torque measurement setup. Experimental characterization revealed strong periodic dependencies between mover position, current excitation, and the resulting parasitic forces and torques along the magnetic pitch of the motor. Based on these observations, an analytical model was developed to describe the dominant pitch torque behaviour and was subsequently used to generate a compensation map integrated into the control system through additional current injection strategies. The proposed compensation approach demonstrated a reduction in the measured pitch torque while maintaining stable motor operation. The results provide a practical framework for the analysis and compensation of parasitic effects in LPMSM systems and establish a foundation for future developments in high-precision motion control applications.

projects.title: Between technology and therapy: How design, motivation, and user insights can strengthen retention in digital treatment programs
projects.abstract:
Mental health disorders are among the most prevalent and costly public health challenges in Denmark, and digital treatment programmes have increasingly been positioned as a scalable response to growing demand for psychological support. This thesis examines how digital treatment programmes with psychological support can be designed and arranged at the Center for Digital Psychiatry (CEDIP) to promote patient retention.
The study begins with a quick overlook of how the digital treatments at CEDIP works, alongside explanations of their creation. Here some constraints are also explained. After this the study draws on a qualitative mix-method design, combining participant observation during a development sprint, individual interviews with two former patients, and two group interviews with professionals. The empirical material is analysed across three sections, each guided by a distinct theoretical framework. First is a critical perspective on motivation of patients informed by Kousholt, Krejsler, and Nissen's (2019) book ‘At skulle ville’. Second is a design analysis based on Donald Norman's (1999) concepts of affordances, constraints, and conventions. Third is a look at the organisational aspect of creating digital treatment programs by Wanda Orlikowski's (2000) ‘practice lens’.
The analysis reveals three main findings. First, patients' motivation is far more situated and dynamic than conventionally thought. Rather than arriving with a stable motivational state, patients' engagement is continuously shaped in interaction with the programme and their surrounding context - challenging the assumption that a sudden lack of inner motivation is what drives lack of retention. Second, the programme's design and language are not neutral: choices about navigation, module structure, login procedures, and tone constitute a communicative affordance layer that can either support or undermine retention. Breakdowns between real and perceived affordance risk eroding patient trust in the programme as a whole. Third, the development of treatment content is shaped by significant interpretive, technological, and institutional constraints. The platform affords limited design flexibility, practitioners express uncertainty about who the target user actually is, and clinical psychology remains the dominant reference point in development, leaving other forms of expertise underutilised.
Based on these findings, the thesis recommends that CEDIP strengthen cross-disciplinary involvement in programme development, establish a shared content manual, invest in systematic user research, and work more deliberately with the motivational technologies embedded in the programme - particularly the timing and proactivity of psychologist contact. The thesis concludes that retention cannot be reduced to patient motivation alone, nor to design quality alone, but emerges in the ongoing interaction between patient, programme, and organisation.

projects.title: Analysis of Wave Propagation in Conical Wind Turbine Tower
projects.abstract: This thesis investigates wave propagation and vibro-acoustic behaviour in a conical wind turbine tower. The study integrates the Wave Finite Element Method (WFEM) with an energy balance principle, the analytical WKB approximation, and an ANSYS finite element model. Two excitation frequencies, 106.25 Hz and 504 Hz, are identified from experimental data as dominant contributions. The WFEM implementation is validated using simplified cylindrical and solid conical geometries before being applied to a conical shell tower. Results are obtained for wave mode 0, showing good agreement between WFEM, WKB, and FE models. The influence of structural wave propagation on radiated noise is analysed, highlighting the effects of geometric variation and local structural modifications on dispersion behaviour and amplitude distribution.

GeoAI-based Afforestation Suitability Screening
projects.abstract:
This project investigates how a GeoAI-based screening workflow can support early-stage afforestation planning in Viborg Municipality, Denmark. The workflow combines rule-based eligibility screening with machine-learning-based suitability modelling, spatial validation, model interpretation, and planning-oriented map outputs.

Legal, environmental, and planning-related constraints are first used to define the eligible decision space. Within this area, LightGBM, Random Forest, and PU-LightGBM are applied to rank potential afforestation areas based on geospatial predictors such as terrain, hydrology, soil type, nitrogen retention, land cover, and landscape context. The models are evaluated using spatial cross-validation to assess geographic transferability.

The results show that GeoAI can provide a transparent and reproducible screening layer for identifying areas where further afforestation assessment may be relevant. The workflow does not replace municipal planning judgement, landowner dialogue, or formal approval processes, but can support the prioritisation of candidate areas under the Danish Green Tripartite framework.
