projects.title: "I don´t have a good enough idea of what it could be like. To even hope" - A qualitative study of young people with autism and their experiences of the transition to adulthood in STU contexs.
projects.abstract:
This thesis explores how young people with autism experience the transition to adult
hood in STU contexts (Særligt Tilrettelagt Ungdomsuddannelse, Specially Organized
Youth Education) and how normative expectations shape these experiences. The re
search question was explored through a critical phenomenological framework, using
participant observations in two STU contexts and semistructured interviews with five
students. Through Reflexive Thematic Analysis, three themes were identified: Be
tween independence and dependence, gradual experiences with adulthood and Be
tween hope and uncertainty. The analysis shows that the participants experience the
transition to adulthood as a gradual and continuous process without clear ruptures,
while simultaneously orienting themselves towards the changes, demands and norma
tive expectations associated with adulthood, which are also embedded within the STU
contexts. The STU contexts thus emerge as institutional settings in which normative
expectations of adulthood are made visible, reproduced, and at times negotiated. In
particular, expectations of independence are prominent both within STU institutions
and in the participants´ own descriptions. Independence appears both as an aspiration
and as something the young people negotiate in relation to their life situations, making
it both a normative ideal and a dynamic and contextual construct. The findings high
light that dependence, support and relations are integrated into the participants´ under
standing of independence, which supports the crip-theoretical concept of interdepend
ence as a relevant framework for STU contexts and psychological practice, as it may
help legitimize support needs, relationality and dependence as valid adult positions.
Another key finding is that the young people experience their future as uncertain and
marked by concerns. The analysis points to a tension within the STU contexts, where
the students are expected to orient themselves towards adulthood, while the staff are
not necessarily able to provide answers regarding future opportunities and sometimes
appear hesitant to engage with the young people´s concerns. The absence of
knowledge about concrete future opportunities may limit the participants access to the
real-possible, and, consequently, their capacity to develop concrete hopes. To support
the young people’s sense of hope, the thesis proposes that pedagogical and psycholog
ical practices allow space for dialogue about future possibilities and uncertainties,
which is particularly relevant for young people with autism, for whom the transition
to adulthood is often non-linear. However, the study does not include interviews with
staff, meaning that their perspectives and conditions for supporting the young people´s
hopes and future orientations remain underexplored and call for further investigation
in future research.

projects.title: An Investigation of Caretaking & Accessibility in the Archival Practice of the Danish Arctic Institute
projects.abstract: This thesis examines the often debated role of Danish archives, as pertains to the release and digitalization of especially delicate, or sensitive, records, such as those that show a colonial or exploitative past. Through this examination much emphasis is placed on the balance between a classic archival practice, where the archivist must focus on an imagined neutrality and objectivity through the narratives of the records, and a practice more empathetic and mindful to the needs of those marginalised by historical narratives. This is particularly observed through the methods employed at the Danish Arctic Institute, an organization that works with records picturing the Danish state's relationship with Greenland, a relationship that often results in sensitive material, such as colonial exploitation or other more delicate subjects. As such, this institution has served as an example of mindfulness in the use of appraisal, digitalization, metadata and the reconstruction of provenance. The Danish Arctic Institute manages to show how archives are able to effectively show mindfulness while, not only, retaining the ability to efficiently follow archival protocol but also earning trust from both the marginalised or affected groups and other peer archives.

projects.title: Active Vibration Control of WTG
projects.abstract:
Wind turbine gearboxes are exposed to high-frequency torsional vibrations caused by gear meshing, which can lead to increased wear and reduced efficiency over time. This thesis investigates how these mesh order vibrations can be modelled and reduced through active control using generator torque.
A frequency and order-domain analysis of measured vibration data is used to identify the main excitation mechanisms in a two-stage planetary gearbox. Based on this, a simplified Single Degree of Freedom (SDOF) torsional model is developed using a grey box approach. The model parameters are identified from operational data using nonlinear least-squares optimisation, while time-varying excitation gains are estimated using a sliding-window method. The model captures the key dynamic behaviour, including resonance effects and how vibration levels change with speed and load.
Two control strategies are tested in simulation: Harmonic Feedforward (HFF) and Adaptive Harmonic Feedforward (Adaptive HFF). HFF applies a cancelling torque at the mesh frequency, while Adaptive HFF adjusts this cancellation based on the measured vibration level.
Both methods reduce vibrations under normal conditions, but the adaptive approach performs better when operating conditions vary. In general, this study shows that this approach is useful for reducing vibrations in wind turbine gearboxes.

projects.title: Design, Modeling, and Control of a Two-DOF Seat-Mover Motion Platform for Sim-Racing
projects.abstract:
This thesis presents the design and con-
trol of a two-degree-of-freedom seat-mover
motion application for sim racing. The
system is developed in collaboration with
Asetek SimSports to enhance immersion
by replicating key motion cues from race
car dynamics. A mechanical solution en-
abling independent pitch and roll motion
is proposed and integrated with an exist-
ing cockpit.
The system dynamics are modeled us-
ing the Euler-Lagrange formulation, and a
cascaded control structure is designed to
ensure stable and accurate motion track-
ing. A Motion Cueing Algorithm is im-
plemented to transform vehicle telemetry
into achievable motion cues using tilt co-
ordination principles.
Simulation results indicate that the sys-
tem can reproduce dominant motion sen-
sations within the physical limitations of
the platform. The findings suggest that
the proposed seat-mover design is a viable
and efficient alternative to more complex
motion systems, although further work is
required to complete software implemen-
tation and experimental validation.

projects.title: A Study on the Asset Administration Shell (AAS) and its Benefits to Simulations
projects.abstract: This thesis investigates whether the Asset Administration Shell (AAS) can serve as a structured parameter source for kinematic robot simulation, improving fidelity over conventional manually configured approaches. The work was conducted in collaboration with Danfoss as a laboratory case study at Aalborg University using a Universal Robots UR3 collaborative arm. A digital twin pipeline was implemented integrating thr UR3 AAS representation, a Docker-deployed BaSyx AAS server, the URSim kinematic simulator, and a Streamlit web application for result monitoring and cross-pipeline analysis. A quasi-experimental design compares the real robot's performance with AAS and non-AAS enabled simulations. The report presents the system architecture, implementation details, experimental evaluation, discussion of the obtained results, and reflections on the limitations and future potential of AAS-driven digital twin systems. The results demonstrate that AAS-driven parameter delivery functions correctly end-to-end, and that the principal constraint on simulation fidelity improvement is the simulator's parameter interface rather than the AAS architecture.

projects.title: Leadership in the Cross-Pressure Between State and Culture: An Examination of School Leadership in Danish Minority Schools in South Schleswig
projects.abstract:
This thesis examines how school leaders at Danish minority schools in Southern Schleswig experience and manage tensions arising from competing organizational, cultural, and institutional demands. Using Duborg-Skolen as case, the thesis analyses how school leadership navigates the tension between German educational legislation and the Danish minority’s objective of preserving and promoting Danish language, culture, and identity.
The theoretical framework draws on research concerning tensions in border regions and minority schools, as well as on the theory of paradox leadership, with particular emphasis on types of paradoxes and paradox management strategies. Methodologically, the study adopts a qualitative, deductive, and hermeneutically inspired case study approach based on semi-structured interviews with four members of the school’s leadership team. The analysis investigates both the tensions experienced by the leaders and the ways in which these tensions are managed in practice, before synthesizing the central analytical findings in a concluding display.
The empirical findings demonstrate that the school leaders experience a persistent tension between German legislation and governance logics on the one hand, and Danish culture and pedagogical traditions on the other. These tensions are particularly evident in relation to legal and regulatory requirements, cultural and linguistic considerations, financial and organizational frameworks, and differing national governance logics. In particular, the balance between German governance and standardization and the minority schools’ distinctive cultural position emerges as a central concern in leadership practice. At the same time, the analysis shows that the leaders do not seek to eliminate these tensions; rather, they actively engage with them through various forms of paradox management, including compromise, transcendence, neutralization, and prioritization.
The thesis concludes that school leadership in Danish minority schools in Southern Schleswig is characterized by a complex and continuous balancing act between competing considerations, in which paradox leadership constitutes a relevant analytical framework for understanding leadership practices. The study thus contributes insight into how leadership practices are shaped within Duborg-Skolen as a Danish minority school operating at the intersection of national, cultural, and institutional logics. Furthermore, the thesis highlights the need for further research into the tensions arising between German legislation and Danish culture in other minority schools, as well as the opportunities associated with applying paradox leadership theory to the study of minority institutions.

projects.title: Design and Optimisation of Passive Damping Mechanisms for Solar Array Deployment
projects.abstract: This project extends previous investigations into damping mechanisms for solar array deployment systems. The objective is to develop and evaluate damper concepts capable of providing the energy dissipation required for controlled solar panel deployment. Viscoelastic damping is first assessed through creep-induced deformation using two space-qualified elastomer materials. The analysis indicates that viscoelastic damping is not a viable solution for applications subjected to uncontrolled thermal environments due to its strong dependence on temperature. Subsequently, a damping concept based on elastic deformation and frictional dissipation is developed and optimised, resulting in four candidate designs. Although convergence issues prevented the finite element contact simulations from producing reliable frictional dissipation results for the optimised configurations, the underlying methodology is validated using representative non-optimised designs. The numerical results demonstrate strong agreement between analytical predictions and finite element simulations, supporting the validity of the proposed approach and indicating the potential feasibility of deformation and friction-based damping for solar array deployment applications. Future work includes improved numerical contact modelling, experimental validation of the proposed concepts, and the development of a generalised design formulation for friction and deformation-based hinge dampers.

Enabling Controlled Reasoning Capabilities for LLMs in the Healthcare Diagnostic Process Using KG-RAG
projects.abstract: Through an experiment of a CDSS with KG-RAG this paper seeks to understand its influence and performance relative to the potential of a simple LLM. LLMs carry potential in assisting the diagnosing process, but are not common proactive due to drawbacks like: hidden logic, hallucination, etc. The approach is called an In silico experiment and it is cross-sectional in this use case. The goal of the experiment is to isolate tendencies within the population of general diagnosis processes by introducing a low-effort tool for support. The sample is 66 synthetically generated notes and these are tested with varying prompts. The hypotheses proposed focus on label precision on final diagnosis and the systems adherence to instructions, and are tested through LLM judges and reasoning elaboration, resulting in falsification and verification respectively. Precision of the KG-RAG system underperforms relative to No-RAG alternatives, however a high degree of fidelity is found in compliance of the output relative to source material. This concludes in a rejection of the hypothesis of precision and acceptance of the hypothesis of control. The paper finds that by integrating KG-RAG into an LLM-based CDSS control is achieved, however lowers precision.

The Sustainability Paradox - ESG Pressures and Supply Chain Trade-Offs in the Cosmetic Industry
projects.abstract:
This research is conducted as a master’s thesis by Alexander Østergaard Hansen, student of M.Sc
International Business at Aalborg University Business School. This research paper investigates
how ESG pressures create trade-offs on the supply chain resilience of the cosmetic industry, using
Danish hybrid CDMO DermaPharm A/S as the basis for the case study. Based on a comprehensive
collection of obtained qualitative data gained through interviews, an analysis and exploration were
conducted on the collected findings, to identify the main ESG trade-offs that are affecting
DermaPharm's supply chain resilience.
The research applies an abductive approach grounded in critical realism, using institutional theory,
global value chain analysis, stakeholder theory, and the resource-based view as key analytical
frameworks to examine the internal capabilities and external pressures that shape DermaPharm
A/S's ESG position within the cosmetic value chain.
The main trade-offs identified include structural trade-offs stemming from DermaPharm’s mid-
tier position in the fragmented cosmetic GVC, client-driven ESG pressures arising from the
unpredictable and mimetic nature of B2B demands, and the challenges related to ESG data
credibility stemming from unverifiable emission data across the value chain. These findings
provide a new empirical insight into the under-researched topic of mid-tier hybrid CDMO
operators in the cosmetic sector, revealing that proactive ESG integration is key in navigating
times of shifting regulations, however, it does not result in the elimination of all supply chain trade-
offs.

projects.title: Optimized production and prebiotic uses of sulfonolipids
projects.abstract:
Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) affects 2.5–3
million individuals in Europe and is associated
with chronic inflammation of the gastrointesti
nal tract. Although its etiology is not fully
understood, both genetic factors and shifts in
the gut microbiome’s microbial diversity, sulfur
metabolism, and the presence of specific bacte
rial taxa play an important role in IBD. Modulat
ing the microbiome through diet or prebiotics is
therefore a promising strategy for improving gut
health. Sulfonolipids (Sols) have emerged as po
tential anti-inflammatory compounds, but their
production and effects on the microbiome remain
unclear. In this study, Sol production was op
timized using Flavobacterium johnsoniae (Fjoh),
with CYE medium supplemented with 0.5 g/L
cysteate yielding increased biomass and Sol pro
duction. Fjoh was shown to produce a Sol pro
file similar to that of the gut-associated genus
Alistipes. The effects of Sols were tested by in
cubating pooled human stool samples with ex
tracted lipids. Sol supplementation significantly
increased hydrogen sulfide (H2S) production but
did not consistently affect short-chain fatty acid
(SCFA) levels, as measured by capillary elec
trophoresis and quantitative NMR. Furthermore,
16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing showed no
significant changes in microbial diversity, and
quantitative PCR analysis indicated no effect on
the absolute abundance of Alistipes. Overall,
while Sols can influence microbial metabolism,
particularly by increasing H2S production, they
do not substantially alter microbiome composi
tion or SCFA production under the tested condi
tions.

projects.title: Ready, Set, Go Between Stabilization and Positioning - A CCO Analysis of the Center for Biosolutions
projects.abstract:
Summary
This thesis examines the communicative constitution of Center for Biosolutions DTU (CFB), a newly established coordinating unit at the Technical University of Denmark, during its formation process from November 2025 to June 2026. Drawing on a Communication Constitutes Organization (CCO) perspective, primarily rooted in the Montreal School, the study investigates what the stabilization, or lack thereof, of the center reveals about its readiness for external positioning ahead of its planned launch in the summer of 2026.
The study adopts a qualitative case study design and draws on document analysis, email correspondence, semi structured interviews, observations, and survey data. The empirical material is analysed through a CCO lens, with particular attention to the interaction between conversation and text, the exercise of epistemic and deontic authority, and the ongoing tension between organization and disorganization.
The analysis follows thirteen communicative moments across internal documents, email correspondence, interviews, and observations, tracing how CFB gradually takes shape through an interplay between conversation and text. The findings show that stabilization is primarily textual. CFB appears as a coherent and anchored organization in strategic documents, meeting minutes, and communication materials, while this stabilization is not fully recognized in the operational reality described by organizational actors. Stabilization therefore emerges not as a final organizational state, but as a temporary and reversible accomplishment continuously subject to renegotiation.
Drawing on Putnam et al.'s constitutive paradox theory, the thesis identifies five structural paradoxes emerging through the constitution process: the performing paradox, the financing paradox, the key person dependency paradox, the fragmentation and autonomy paradox, and the communication paradox. These paradoxes are not understood as problems to be solved, but as dialectical tensions that must be navigated as ongoing conditions of organizational existence.
The thesis concludes that organizational readiness for external positioning cannot be answered with a simple yes or no. Positioning does not follow from stabilization. It is itself part of the stabilization process. CFB will launch not because it is fully stabilized, but because competitive pressure and timing demand it. From a CCO perspective, dis/organization is not a temporary condition that disappears once an organization is launched. Rather, it constitutes a fundamental feature of organizing itself. The study therefore contributes to discussions of organizational positioning by demonstrating how external positioning may occur despite the continued presence of internal instability and unresolved tensions.

projects.title: Brand relevance in an algorithm-driven media landscape
projects.abstract:
This thesis investigates how a locally embedded jewellery business can build brand relevance
among young adults in a social media environment characterized by attention competition
and platform-specific visibility logics, when the product itself is one of low daily actuality.
The study is conducted as a qualitative case study of Aabybro Guld & Sølv, a small
family-owned jeweller in northern Denmark, and addresses a wider communicative
challenge: how small, locally embedded businesses with limited resources can establish brand
relevance before a concrete consumer need arises, in a digital media environment where
visibility depends on both algorithmic prioritization and user interpretation.
Theoretically, the thesis combines perspectives on relational branding (Fournier,
1998; Keller, 2001; Holt, 2004), attention as a scarce resource (Simon, 1971; Citton, 2017),
and social media logics (Bucher, 2012; Kietzmann et al., 2011) with Andersen and
Smedegaard’s (2014) communication-plannning model, Diamanten. The analysis is grounded
in a social constructivist epistemology (Burr, 2015), where meaning is understood as
constructed in the encounter between sender and receiver rather than as an inherent property
of communication.
Empirically, the study draws on four qualitative interviews, one with the company’s
owners and three with young adults aged 23-26, and a multimodal analysis (Lemke, 2009) of
seven Facebook posts, examining the relationship between verbal text and visual imagery.
The analysis identifies three central findings. First, the company’s communication
operates across three incompatible semiotic registers, a dominant relational register, a
sales-oriented register, and a reel-based register, that do not cohere into a single brand
narrative. The relational posts make verbal claims about kinship, craftsmanship, and
affection, but visually present products in a decontextualized catalog register, producing a
text-image gap that weakens the relational story. Second, applying Kietzmann et al.’s
honeycomb model reveals a misalignment between the building blocks the company activates
(primarily identity and reputation) and those through which the target group actually engages
(conversations, sharing, and presence). The company speaks in the blocks where the audience
does not act and remains silent in the blocks where they do. Third, brand relevance is not
achieved through increased content production or imitation of larger commercial brands, but
through three coherent communicative movements: closing the text-image gap, consolidating
the registers into a recognizable brand position, and activating the visibility logics,
Anne Sofie Tram Aalborg Universitet 1. juni 2026
4. semester Kommunikation Kandidatspeciale
particularly network-based and engagement-based logics, to which the company’s local and
relational character is best suited.
A central strategic insight is that the company’s actual differentiation lies not in
relational storytelling, which many local businesses use, but in its circular craft practice,
remelting heirloom gold, reusing customers’ stones, repairing rather than discarding, and
refining workshop waste, which the company already practices but does not communicate.
Brand relevance, there, is not about inventing a distinct position, but about making an
existing and authentic practice communicatively visible through what the thesis terms process
transparency: showing transformation rather than asserting presence.
The thesis contributes to existing research on small business communication by
demonstrating how brand relevance, attention economics, and organizational conditions
intersect in a single case, and how a coherent communicative position can emerge from latent
organizational practice rather than from increased communicative output.

Between Structure and Practice - A Study of Knowledge Sharing, Document Management, and Organizational Continuity At Cimbria A/S
projects.abstract:
This thesis investigates how employees’ practices for internal and external knowledge sharing and document management are supported and challenged across organizational units. The study is based on a qualitative case study of Cimbria A/S, where SharePoint, Salesforce and related systems are used to support documentation, project coordination and information sharing throughout organizational workflows.

Through qualitative interviews, the thesis examines how employees work with documentation, knowledge sharing and information management in their daily practices, and how knowledge and information move between departments, project phases and organizational functions. The analysis shows that documentation is not merely a matter of storing information, but is closely connected to local work practices, departmental routines and organizational knowledge flows. Although formal structures for documentation and information sharing are established, information is not necessarily interpreted, transferred or reused consistently across departments and project phases.

The thesis applies Wenger’s theory of Communities of Practice and Nonaka’s SECI model to analyze how knowledge is shared, transformed and embedded in organizational workflows. The findings show that organizational knowledge sharing is shaped by local practices, experience-based learning and cross-departmental coordination. Knowledge transfer is therefore not a linear process, but involves continuous interpretation, reconstruction and translation of information between organizational communities of practice.

Based on these findings, the thesis identifies a number of design opportunities aimed at strengthening continuity, traceability and reuse of organizational knowledge. These include standardized handover processes, practice-oriented onboarding, cross-departmental knowledge sharing, shared reference projects and AI-supported information retrieval. The thesis concludes that effective knowledge sharing and document management depend not only on formal systems and documentation structures, but on the interaction between organizational practices, social knowledge processes and the technological environments in which employees work.

Unified Digital Platform for Managing Advanced Technology Assets at Novo Nordisk
projects.abstract:
This thesis investigates how existing equipment-related practices and coordination workflows within the Advanced Technology Development Team (ATDT) at Novo Nordisk can be understood and supported through the development of a unified digital platform for advanced technology asset management. The project was motivated by recurring challenges related to equipment visibility, fragmented storage practices, reliance on informal communication, and the absence of a shared overview of available equipment. These challenges often made it difficult for employees to locate, access, and coordinate the use of advanced technology assets across the team.
The study follows an exploratory and qualitative research approach grounded in an interpretive understanding of organisational practices. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, observations, contextual walkthroughs, workshops, and usability testing activities conducted within the organisational environment. The project combined empirical investigation with iterative concept development and the implementation of a functional prototype using Microsoft Power Apps and SharePoint.
The findings show that equipment management within ATDT extends beyond simple inventory tracking and is closely connected to everyday work practices, collaboration routines, physical workspace organisation, and shared responsibility for maintaining equipment information. Participants frequently relied on personal experience and informal communication when locating equipment, while inconsistent storage practices and limited visibility created challenges related to accessibility, coordination, and trust in available information.
Based on these findings, a set of design requirements was developed and translated into an early-stage functional prototype. The proposed platform provides a searchable overview of equipment, supports access to technical information, enables basic booking and coordination activities, and allows users to register and manage assets through a shared digital environment. The prototype was evaluated with representative users from the organisational setting through usability testing and feedback sessions.
The evaluation indicated that users generally perceived the platform as relevant and useful for improving equipment visibility and coordination. The findings highlighted the importance of simplicity, intuitive navigation, clear information structures, and alignment with existing work practices. The evaluation also emphasised that successful implementation depends not only on technical functionality but also on organisational factors such as maintenance routines, data quality, governance structures, and user engagement.
The thesis concludes that internal equipment management systems may provide value not only as repositories of information but also as coordination-oriented organisational platforms that support visibility, accessibility, and collaboration. Furthermore, the project demonstrates that effective equipment management requires alignment between digital systems, physical workspace organisation, and existing organisational practices. The developed prototype provides an initial proof of concept and establishes a foundation for future development, broader organisational adoption, and continued integration of digital and physical coordination mechanisms within Novo Nordisk.

In the Passenger: Seat Negotiating Professional Identity, Gender Expectations, and Structural Barriers Among Highly Educated Trailing Spouses in North Denmark
projects.abstract:
This thesis explores the lived experiences and integration processes of highly educated international women who migrate to North Denmark as trailing spouses. Grounded in a social constructivist, interpretivist, and critical feminist paradigm, the study employs a qualitative and abductive research approach. Data was collected through in-depth biographical narrative interviews with eight highly educated international women living in North Denmark. The analysis was conducted systematically using thematic coding to capture both collective patterns and unique individual nuances.The dual theoretical framework combines Pierre Bourdieu’s sociology of capital, field, and habitus with Axel Honneth’s theory of recognition. Bourdieu’s concepts help analyze why the women's foreign qualifications and social networks are often devalued or difficult to convert into local symbolic capital. Honneth’s three spheres of recognition (love, rights, and solidarity) explain the reduced self-esteem, and invisibility resulting from labor market exclusion.
The findings introduce the Click-Experience Model, demonstrating that long-term retention is driven not by time, but by a subjective psychological turning point (the click-experience) triggered by objective milestones such as relevant employment, social recognition, and children’s well-being. The analysis reveals that the regional Danish labor market operates as a relatively closed field where foreign qualifications are frequently devalued, leading to occupational downshifting and financial dependence. To restore legitimacy within the household, many women experience a process of refeminization, compensating through increased domestic labor. Furthermore, the study identifies a sharp intersectional divergence in social integration: while motherhood acts as a "social bridge" to Danish networks via childcare institutions, childless women often rely on a fragile, "borrowed social identity" mediated through their partner. This marginalization is further intensified for non-EU women due to cultural distance, language barriers, and legal dependency. The study highlights that labor market integration is not merely a matter of individual qualifications, but is heavily governed by unequal social capital and regional structures of recognition. It states that the transition into a trailing spouse role fundamentally challenges the women's autonomy.

projects.title: Integrating Agentic AI with ERP Systems for Project-Based Recruitment - A Sociotechnical Framework for Fair Candidate Screening System Evaluated Through Empirical Audit of Gender Bias in Embedding and LLM
projects.abstract:
Plant Supervision, a Danish project-based recruitment firm, runs candidate searches as keyword filters over an internal CV database followed by recruiter-relationship shortlisting, a workflow that is slow under a competitive market and structurally biased against candidates without prior engagement history. HireX, an agentic AI screener built on the firm’s database, was developed to address both through embedding-based retrieval and a LangGraph-orchestrated language-model screener, however whether it delivers fairer recruitment than the workflow it replaces, under the responsible-AI obligations of an EU-deployed high-risk system, had not been measured before this thesis began. We audit HireX through Sociotechnical Systems Theory across eight research questions to find the joint optimized configuration, using 485 paired counterfactual male and female CVs at three writing-style intensity
levels, with a configuration sweep over embedding strategy and model, input format, prompting strategy, language model and the presence of a bias-aware audit agent, and we measure bias with Statistical Parity Difference, Disparate Impact, Counterfactual Fairness Gap and its exposure-weighted variant. The findings show that Gender is recoverable from anonymized resumes, section-wise embedding strategy is the most biased retrieval onfiguration,
full job descriptions reduce retrieval bias over title-only queries, and writing-style divergence amplifies bias even in fairer configurations. The recommended deployment combines full-text MPNet retrieval on anonymized CVs, full job descriptions as queries, the baseline screening prompt on GPT-4.1- nano with anonymized labels and no separate audit agent in the advisory recruiter-in-the-loop agentic AI framework, and API based Maconomy integration. Evidently, Joint optimized configuration provided responsible agentic AI application integration with ERP system framework ensuring both technical and social subsystem optimization.

projects.title: Mentoring Under Organizational Pressures: How Nurses as Frontline Workers balance the Training of Newly Recruited Nurses in a Hospital Ward in North Jutland
projects.abstract:
This thesis examines how nurse mentors and development nurses interpret and balance the training of newly recruited nurses in a hospital ward in North Jutland.
The study is prompted by the challenges facing the healthcare sector with nursing shortage and lack of nursing care. Existing research highlights mentoring programmes as a key initiative in fostering nurses’ connection to the profession and their clinical skills. At the same time, research highlights the challenge of implementing mentoring programmes as intended in a hospital setting.
The study design is based on a qualitative case study conducted in a somatic hospital ward in the North Jutland Region. The empirical data for the thesis comprises local induction documents and semi-structured interviews with a development nurse and three nurse mentors. Methodologically, an abductive approach is adopted, in which the dialectic between theory and empirical evidence underpins the hermeneutic foundation of the thesis. The theoretical framework of this thesis is based on the work of Michael Lipsky, Lars Tummers et al. and Margaret Wetherwell. In this thesis, mentors and development nurse are viewed as frontline staff who navigate between organisational demands, limited resources and the ideal of supporting the learning of the newly recruited nurses, whilst performing their own duties and ensuring the quality of nursing care.
The thesis concludes that the training of newly recruited nurses is shaped by frontline staff balancing rationing, routinisation and affective practices in their work with different types of client needs. The development nurse places greater emphasis on the mentor’s personal qualities than on the mentor’s professional skills and downplays the need for resources. Mentors have to balance patient care with training new staff within a dynamic and unpredictable environment, where the pressure of a busy workload means that reflection is put on hold and mentoring takes a back seat. The relationship between the mentor and the new recruit is seen as significant in terms of the learning opportunities the mentor provides for the new recruit. With a view to promoting engagement, clinical competence and quality in the nursing profession, the findings of this thesis may warrant further investigation into structural conditions and the significance of professional identity for the relationship between mentors and newly recruited nurses.

projects.title: I know I'm being wronged, but what can I do about it
projects.abstract:
Abstract
Trade unions have historically played a central role in securing and improving workers’ rights in Denmark. However, declining membership rates and changing labour market conditions have raised questions about the continued relevance of trade unions and their ability to communicate their value to both current and potential members. This thesis examines how trade unions communicate workers’ rights and membership-related benefits in practice, with particular attention to the role of shop stewards as mediators of information and knowledge.
The study is based on a qualitative case study of the Danish trade union 3F. Empirical data consist of three semi-structured interviews with individuals occupying different positions within the organisation, including a shop steward, a union representative involved in training activities, and an employee working with communication and outreach initiatives. In addition, the study includes observations from a public information event concerning occupational injuries and an analysis of selected communication materials produced by 3F.
The theoretical framework combines Knud Illeris’ theory of learning with literature on the education and development of shop stewards. Furthermore, the study is informed by a social constructivist perspective, emphasising how meaning and knowledge are created through social interaction and communication processes.
The findings indicate that trade unions utilise multiple communication channels, including digital platforms, printed materials, educational activities, and direct interpersonal communication. While digital communication provides broad access to information, it often requires members to actively seek out and engage with available resources. In contrast, shop stewards function as accessible and trusted intermediaries who translate complex legal and collective agreement-related information into forms that are meaningful and relevant to employees’ everyday working lives.
The analysis highlights the importance of personal communication in supporting learning and understanding. Through dialogue, shared experiences, and contextualised explanations, shop stewards contribute not only to the dissemination of information but also to members’ learning processes. Illeris’ concepts of interaction, content, and motivation help explain why interpersonal communication often appears more effective than purely informational approaches. The findings further suggest that the effectiveness of communication is closely linked to the competencies, engagement, and local workplace context of individual shop stewards.
The thesis concludes that shop stewards remain a key component of trade union communication and play a significant role in helping workers understand and utilise their rights. Although digital communication tools are increasingly important, personal interaction continues to be crucial for creating engagement, understanding, and meaningful learning. The study therefore points to the continued importance of education, competence development, and organisational support for shop stewards in maintaining the relevance of trade unions in a changing labour market.

projects.title: A Master thesis on Strategic Framework for Human-AI collaboration in Digital Manufacturing
projects.abstract:
This master thesis examines how human-AI collaboration can be structured to improve decision-making, operational performance, and system resilience in digital manufacturing. Focusing on Varsun Aerospace Technologies, the study explores how AI can support human expertise in a high-precision aerospace manufacturing environment undergoing digital transformation. The research is grounded in augmented intelligence theory and the automation-augmentation paradox, emphasizing that AI should complement rather than replace human decision-making.
A qualitative single-case study approach was applied using semi-structured interviews, internal documents, and observational insights. The findings show that effective human-AI collaboration can enhance decision quality by combining data-driven insights with human judgment, while also improving operational flexibility and responsiveness. At the same time, human oversight remains essential for managing uncertainty, system limitations, and unexpected disruptions.
Based on these findings, the study proposes a human-centric AI integration framework consisting of four key elements: task allocation, decision authority, trust calibration, and continuous learning. The framework provides a structured approach for balancing automation with human expertise in manufacturing contexts. The thesis contributes to the literature by offering a context-specific and practical model for implementing sustainable human-AI collaboration in digital manufacturing.

projects.title: Our new friend? A critical-theoretical analysis of the rationales behind generative AI in postmodern working life
projects.abstract:
Generative AI has globally seen a substantial growth in interest and implementation both in private and professional contexts. Since the launch of ChatGPT in 2022 this field has attracted enormous attention, creating a phenomenon in generative AI and Large Language Models (LLM) which in today’s society is omnipresent and almost impossible to avoid. Generative AI has become increasingly prevalent in the Danish labor market. Seven out of ten companies in Denmark report using generative AI within work related operations. For this technology to be implemented and used responsibly, the European Union has in 2024 released the EU AI Act, which has contributed to our interest in conducting this study.
Using Hartmut Rosa’s theory of social acceleration and his perspective on the conditions for a fulfilling working life, this thesis examines the rationales behind implementing generative AI within the P&C management of a selected global company, operating in a late-modern and highly competitive landscape.
The study was conducted from a critical-theoretical perspective, using qualitative interviews with P&C-managers from a company, as well as a guiding expert interview and a document analysis of the EU AI Act, to gather knowledge on the subject area.
The focus of our analysis has been to illuminate underlying rationales shaping our participants’ decision-making processes relating to the subject matter of this thesis, the company’s implementation of generative AI.
Here we detect a predominant enthusiasm and optimism toward the technology's potential, which is expressed through an anthropomorphic tendency, whereby managers attribute human characteristics to the LLM, describing it as a ‘good friend’. This creates an emotional attachment without genuine reciprocity, which theoretically may condition alienation. P&C-management further positions the LLM as a solution to existing work pressure, based on a latent ‘promise’ of efficiency and time savings. However, analysed through Rosa's theory of social acceleration, technological acceleration does not reduce work load but rather creates conditions for doing more work within the same time frame. This represents a fundamental tension between management's assumed rationale and the theoretical framework. Finally, the implementation is driven by a competitive and economic rationale, whereby generative AI is considered a prerequisite for remaining relevant and retaining one's competitive position.
Our thesis provides insight into how processes can be understood from the perspective of management thinking within a global company, including the explicit and implicit assumptions regarding what LLMs can contribute with, as well as the complexity associated with their implementation. As such, our thesis provides an opportunity to actively pause and reflect on current social tendencies in our society.

projects.title: Juveniles convicted under section 235 of the Danish Criminal Code: A content analysis of juvenile involvement in sexual material depicting individuals under the age of 18
projects.abstract:
In recent years, the number of convictions of 15- to 17-year-olds for sexual offences against
children has more than doubled in Denmark. A substantial part of this increase is attributable
to offences under section 235 of the Danish Criminal Code, which criminalises the distribution
and possession of sexual material depicting individuals under the age of 18. Existing research
on juveniles’ involvement in such material is divided across separate research fields. While
studies on Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM) often emphasise sexual and digital curiosity,
and deliberate involvement, research on image-based sexual abuse (IBSA) among juveniles
increasingly highlights peer relations, digital youth cultures and gendered dynamics. The
literature therefore suggests that such cases must be analysed in relation to the type of material,
the relationship between the parties, the motivation behind the act and the broader social
context in which it occurs.

In response to this, the thesis adopts a developmental and context-sensitive analytical
framework, drawing on Terrie Moffitt’s life-course theory and Situational Action Theory. The
developmental perspective makes it possible to examine whether the acts appear to be linked
to adolescence-specific conditions, or whether they indicate more persistent patterns of
offending. The context-sensitive perspective is used to analyse how social and digital
environments may facilitate and reinforce the young person’s actions by shaping perceived
motivations, normalising certain behaviours and making the distribution or possession of
sexual material appear possible, acceptable or socially rewarding.

Drawing on a qualitative content analysis of court judgments (n=51) concerning 15- to 17-
year-olds convicted under section 235 of the Danish Criminal Code, this thesis finds five
distinct types of behaviour: 1) status-driven distribution, 2) sexually violating positioning, 3)
entertainment-driven distribution, 4) isolated possession, and 5) coercive acquisition. The types
can be placed on a continuum ranging from adolescence-limited behaviour to more persistent
patterns of offending, and they vary in terms of motivation, modes of conduct and degree of
repetition. The thesis argues that this variation is only partly reflected in the legal
consequences. While sentencing allows for individual assessment, registration on the Danish
Child Protection Certificate follows automatically and may therefore unduly label some
juveniles as posing a risk to children, even where the behaviour does not indicate such risk.
The thesis recommends a differentiated model, in which registration for juveniles convicted
under section 235 is based on an individual assessment of whether the case indicates a risk
relevant to the certificate’s protective purpose.

projects.title: Organizational transformation in the context of AI
projects.abstract:
The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly influencing how organizations make decisions, coordinate work processes, and navigate strategic change. While AI is often presented as a technological opportunity capable of improving efficiency, innovation, and decision-making, the technology simultaneously creates new forms of organizational complexity, uncertainty, and adaptation challenges. This thesis investigates how AI’s accelerating development challenges organizational decision-making capacity, and how organizations navigate between strategic adaptation, organizational stability, and employee engagement in AI-related transformation processes.
The study is based on a qualitative case study of an international organization, and draws on semi-structured interviews with employees and actors across different functional areas. The project is grounded in a hermeneutic perspective inspired by Hans-Georg Gadamer and applies an interpretive approach to understanding how AI is experienced, understood, and integrated into organizational practice. The analytical framework combines Karl Weick’s theory of sensemaking with organizational perspectives on coordination, governance, sociotechnical practice, and organizational adaptation.
The analysis demonstrates that AI does not merely function as a technological tool, but as an organizational phenomenon that challenges existing structures, decision-making processes, governance mechanisms, and perceptions of expertise and organizational roles. The findings show that AI accelerates information processing and strategic decision-making, while simultaneously increasing organizational uncertainty, information overload, and the need for coordination and prioritization. The study further highlights how organizations experience tensions between centralized governance and decentralized experimentation, as well as technological acceleration and existing organizational structures.
In addition, the analysis demonstrates that employee engagement in AI-related transformations depends heavily on perceived relevance, organizational meaning, and opportunities for participation and learning. AI is primarily perceived as a technology that complements, rather than replaces human capabilities. However the technology also challenges employees’ understanding of expertise, work identity, and future organizational roles. Organizational adaptation therefore emerges not as a linear implementation process, but as a continuous process of learning, experimentation, and sensemaking.
The thesis concludes that organizations’ primary challenge in relation to AI is not solely technological implementation, but rather their ability to create meaning, coordination, strategic direction, and organizational learning in environments characterized by acceleration, complexity, and continuous uncertainty. AI thereby becomes not only a technological issue, but fundamentally an organizational and human challenge.

projects.title: Democratisation of art through experience design - From cultural policy ideal to institutional practice
projects.abstract:
As art institutions increasingly seek to engage broader audiences, the question arises of how the democratisation of art can move from a cultural policy ideal into institutional practice. This thesis takes Kunsthal Spritten in Aalborg, Denmark, as its case and is based on the institution’s ambition to make contemporary art accessible to more people. Through this case, it explores how IT-based experience design can offer more accessible ways into contemporary art for users without prior knowledge of art.

A central research problem arises from the ambiguity of democratisation as a concept. In cultural institutions, the term is often used as a positive ideal, yet it is not always clear what kind of change it is meant to create for the user. Democratisation is therefore approached as a practice-oriented and context-dependent concept rather than as a fixed objective. Drawing on pragmatism, the concept is understood through the difference it can make in the user’s encounter with the art institution’s spaces and communicative forms. Methodologically, the study is based on desk-based research, a semi-structured interview with Kunsthal Spritten’s director, Bibi Saugman, and a qualitative benchmarking of six art institutions in Copenhagen: Copenhagen Contemporary, Nikolaj Kunsthal, Gammel Strand, MACA Museum, Glyptoteket and Dansk Arkitektur Center. This benchmarking focuses on how technology, aesthetics and communication shape the art experience. The analysis shows that the value of technology cannot be understood through its level of complexity alone. Advanced technological solutions may create powerful sensory and spatial experiences, but they do not necessarily make art more accessible. Conversely, simple digital formats can be valuable when they help the user establish a more meaningful relation to the art. Across the institutions studied, democratisation is mainly addressed by making art easier to access and understand, while the user’s possibility of influencing the experience remains more limited within the standard visitor experience. Based on these findings, a design process is developed with young people aged 20 to 29 in Aalborg Municipality as the target group. This group is selected because it is underrepresented at art institutions and calls for cultural experiences that are more visible and easier to access socially. Five criteria guide the design process: sensory experience, transparency, intuitive use, reflection and integration. Together, these criteria are used to develop and assess four concept proposals, each addressing how the relation between the user and contemporary art might be strengthened.

The final design proposal, Into the Art, combines a physical seating structure with a QR-based audio guide accessed through a clipboard. As a spatial element, the staircase functions as a place where the user can stay, pause and process impressions before, during or after the exhibition. The audio guide adds an auditory layer of mediation, where narrative and sensory elements seek to open up contemporary art without narrowing its space for interpretation. Meanwhile, the clipboard creates a tangible link between the digital mediation and the user’s physical movement through the exhibition. As a contribution, the thesis presents a design proposal that shows how low-complexity technological and spatial design choices can support the user’s conditions for engaging with contemporary art. Into the Art does not give the user direct influence over the content of the art, but it creates better conditions for immersion and personal interpretation. Overall, the thesis concludes that IT-based experience design can contribute to the democratisation of the art experience when technology is used to support the overall experience rather than becoming its primary value. In this understanding, democratisation is not a question of technological intensity, but of developing formats that make contemporary art easier for more people to approach.

When the lions sleep - Development of an experience design that activates guests at the lion enclosure at Aalborg Zoo
projects.abstract:
This thesis explores how experience design can support visitors’ existing fascination with lions and
transform this fascination into meaningful experiences that promote active participation and
strengthen emotional and knowledge-based relationships with the animals. The study is conducted
in collaboration with Aalborg Zoo and focuses on the zoo’s lion enclosure as a case for investigating
how visitor engagement can be enhanced without compromising animal welfare.
The project is grounded in a pragmatic research approach and follows Stanford Design Thinking as
the overall methodological framework. The empirical foundation consists of a literature review,
observations of visitor behaviour, semi-structured interviews with zoo professionals, concept
development, prototyping, and user testing. The findings reveal that visitors are already highly
fascinated by the lions and frequently orient their attention towards the animals. However, this
fascination often remains short-lived and rarely develops into deeper engagement, reflection, or
active use of the zoo’s existing communication initiatives.
Based on these insights, the concept Ranger Command: Protect the Asiatic Lions was developed.
The concept introduces visitors to the role of a Wildlife Ranger and encourages them to observe,
4
interpret, and register lion behaviour through a digital experience. Rather than positioning visitors
as passive recipients of information, the concept seeks to create meaningful participation by
involving them in observation practices inspired by the everyday work of zoo professionals.
User testing indicates that the concept has the potential to increase curiosity, prolong visitor
engagement, and encourage greater attention towards lion behaviour. The findings suggest that
active participation can function as a catalyst for transforming fascination into engagement and
engagement into stronger emotional and knowledge-based relationships with the animals.
Furthermore, the project demonstrates how participatory experience design can support zoological
communication by creating opportunities for visitors to engage more deeply with both the animals
and the conservation efforts that modern zoos represent.
The thesis concludes that experience design based on active participation can strengthen the
relationship between visitors and animals by transforming observation into involvement and
fascination into meaningful engagement.

Working From Home - A Qualitative casestudy about Working From Home
projects.abstract:
This master's thesis examines the concept of working from home and its influence on organizational
processes. The background of the study stems from a specific case in a company that suddenly
announced to its employees that working from home would be withdrawn as of June 1, 2026, so
that everyone from that date would be required to be physically at the office Monday-Friday, which
stood in stark contrast to the rules on working from home prior to this decision. The background for
the decision was officially to strengthen culture, collaboration, and relationships, which motivated
me to investigate the conditions and influence of working from home on these organizational
elements. At the same time, research showed that the topic is highly relevant and currently debated
to an increasing degree.
The study examines 3 research questions: 1) What does existing research highlight about the
relationship between working from home and organizational culture, community & relationships,
and collaboration & knowledge sharing? 2) How do employees experience the influence of working
from home on organizational culture, community & relationships, and collaboration & knowledge
sharing? And 3) How do employees interpret the consequences that a announced withdrawal of the
opportunity to work from home will have on their work and private life?
Methodologically, the thesis utilizes a case study, literature review, and qualitative data collection in
the form of hermeneutic interviews. The literature review resulted in 6 articles, and a total of four
informants were selected and interviewed. The literature review concludes that working from home
has a certain significance for all the described organizational elements. Working from home creates
challenges, particularly in the form of physical absence. In the study's empirical data, a connection
is likewise experienced between working from home and the influence on the organizational
elements. Generally, a connection is seen between physical absence as a source of challenges in
relation to organizational culture, community & relationships, and collaboration & knowledge
sharing. There are, however, nuances to this, and it is experienced differently among the informants,
and for some, there is no experience of, for example, poorer collaboration and knowledge sharing.

When AI listens in - an examination of ambient scribe in clinical practice
projects.abstract:
Indledning: Sundhedsvæsenet oplever overbelastning og stress blandt andet på baggrund af en øget dokumentationsbyrde blandt personalet. Dette speciale undersøger implementeringen af en ambient scribe-løsning, som adresserer disse udfordringer med dokumentations-arbejdet. Ambient scribe er et AI-drevet system, der genererer udkast til patient-journaler ud fra kliniske konsultationer. Specialets formål er at afdække de forandringer teknologien medfølger i dokumentations-processen eller blot forskyder opgaverne og præsenterer nye udfordringer.
Metode: Brugernes oplevelser analyseres gennem kvalitativ data-indsamling af semistrukturerede interviews med syv behandlere i både somatiske og psykiatriske afdelinger i Region Midtjylland. Analysen er udført induktiv og er baseret på meningskondensering, hvor interview-udtalelserne blev tolket og opdelt efter temaer.
Resultater: Resultaterne viser, at størstedelen af deltagerne finder de AI-genererede udkast strukturerede, detaljerige, og at teknologien præsenterer sig som tidsbesparende. Flere deltagere beskrev, at teknologien oplevedes som en mental aflastning, da den reducerede behovet for notatskrivning under konsultationen og fungerede som en hukommelsesstøtte ved udarbejdelse af det endelige journalnotat. Nogle påpegede at ambient scribe gav bedre forudsætning for at journalføre, hvor andre oplevede at behovet for efterredigering præsenterede sig som en barriere for brugen. Fundene viser, at ambient scribe ændrer flowet i konsultationer og introducerer et behov for kvalitetssikring af udkastet, hvilket medfører latente forskydninger i arbejdsgange.
Konklusion: Undersøgelsen fremhæver, at teknologien kan øge journalføringens effektivitet og understøtte fokus til patienten, men pointerer samtidig væsentlige organisatoriske og faglige implikationer. Ambient scribe har potentiale til at effektivisere dokumentations-arbejdet, men at den samtidig introducerer nye udfordringer som kræver opmærksomhed hvis anvendelse af teknologien skal være forsvarlig.

"Anchored in change: An investigation of how startups balance brand authenticity and market adaptation"
projects.abstract:
This thesis investigates how startups balance the need for an authentic and consistent brand identity while adapting to shifting market conditions and emerging trends. The study is motivated by a broader transformation in sustainability discourse, where sustainability has increasingly shifted from being a source of competitive differentiation to becoming a market expectation or hygiene factor. This development creates a strategic challenge for companies whose brands were originally built around sustainability-driven value propositions. The research is based on a qualitative case study of the Danish B2B startup Endless Food Co. (EFC) and its flagship product, THIC (This Isn’t Chocolate), an upcycled chocolate alternative made from side streams from beer production and cocoa shells. The case is particularly relevant because startups operate in a formative phase in which brand identity is often deeply intertwined with founders’ values, networks, and strategic decisions. EFC is currently navigating a transition from sustainability-led communication toward new value propositions centred around supply security and nutritional benefits, raising questions about how market adaptation influences brand authenticity.
The study adopts a social constructivist perspective and applies an inside-out approach to brand identity by focusing on how internal actors construct, negotiate, and articulate the brand. Methodologically, the thesis employs a triangulated qualitative research design consisting of document analysis, qualitative interviews with founders and employees, and an internal workshop. The analysis combines Payne et al.’s (2017) conceptualisation of customer value propositions, Närvänen et al.’s (2021) sociocultural framing approach, and Kapferer’s (2012) Brand Identity Prism to examine the relationship between external market communication and internal identity construction.
The findings suggest that maintaining brand authenticity does not depend on preserving a static value proposition or consistently communicating identical messages over time. Rather, authenticity emerges through alignment between the organisation’s internal identity construction and its external market projections. The case demonstrates that strategic adaptation does not necessarily constitute a break with brand identity, provided that new value propositions can be rooted in the organisation’s existing values and cultural foundations. Furthermore, the study finds that the movement from sustainability toward compliance and resilience represents a process of identity recontextualisation rather than identity replacement. However, the findings also highlight the risks associated with opportunistic trend migration, particularly when external market opportunities are pursued without sufficient internal anchoring.
Finally, the thesis critically reflects the absence of an external stakeholder perspective. Since the analysis primarily focuses on the internal construction of brand identity rather than stakeholder perceptions, the study cannot determine whether intended identity projections translate into corresponding brand images among customers and partners. Consequently, the findings should be understood as contributing to an inside-out understanding of brand authenticity, while also highlighting the need for future research that integrates both identity and image perspectives. Overall, the thesis contributes to branding literature by proposing a process-oriented understanding of brand authenticity and by emphasising the importance of balancing internal identity stability with external adaptability in startup contexts.

From Transparency to Action: How SMEs Translate VSME Reporting into Sustainability Practices
projects.abstract: Sustainability reporting (SR) is the disclosure and communication of information related to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors [European Commission, 2022]. Despite not being obligated to report on their sustainability, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) play a pivotal role in the global economy and the large corporations’ value chains, therefore holding great responsibilities [Sage And International Chamber of Commerce, 2024; OECD, 2025; EFRAG, 2024a]. Focusing on Danish SMEs’ reporting after the Voluntary Sustainability Reporting Standard for non-listed SMEs (VSME), this master thesis examines the connection between SMEs’ VSME reporting and sustainability practices (SP), and whether the process generates knowledge, enables learning and changes to their SPs. The research question How can organisational learning from the VSME reporting process shape sustainability practices in Danish SMEs? is answered through a multiple-case study. This is based on interviews and VSME reports from seven Danish SMEs, and two ESG consultants. The study initially seeks to understand how the cases currently utilise the VSME. This is investigated through the theoretical framework walk-talk-t(w)alk, showing a connection between VSME reporting and SP for all of the cases. However, differences occur in their approach of VSME reporting and how strongly the connection to their SPs is experienced. Furthermore, the SMEs’ learning is analysed through Organisational learning theory, illustrating that SMEs have the possibility to learn and drive SP from the process of VSME reporting. Lastly, factors have been assessed on how the SR can foster SMEs’ learning through their SR processes to utilise the knowledge, go beyond transparency and enhance their SP even further. However, the findings furthermore shows that many external elements outside the SMEs’ scope of influence challenge their ability to learn and enable change from VSME reporting. The thesis concludes that all cases demonstrate a connection between VSME reporting and SP. Learning from the process of VSME reporting shapes SPs in Danish SMEs, though the extent depends on organisational context and engagement with the reporting process.

projects.title: The Influence of Traffic Alarms on Speed and Driver Behaviour - An Empirical Analysis of Speed Data and Self-Reported Behavioural Patterns
projects.abstract:
This thesis investigates how traffic alarms, with a particular focus on Saphe, influences driving speed, behavioural adaptation, and self‑reported risk perception among Danish motorists.
The study combines Floating Car Data collected on selected urban roads, rural roads, school zones, and motorways in combination with a questionnaire survey examining drivers’ self‑assessment, perceived control, and motivations for using traffic alarms. The speed analysis shows that traffic alarms generate clear but short‑lived reductions in speed around enforcement points, while no lasting behavioural changes are observed beyond the immediate vicinity of the alert.
The questionnaire results indicate that many drivers overestimate their driving abilities, underestimate risk, and primarily use traffic alarms to avoid fines rather than to enhance safety. Drivers using traffic alarms also report more frequent speeding compared to those without such devices. The findings suggest that traffic alarms contribute only marginally to long‑term traffic safety and may, in some cases, reinforce risk‑compensatory behaviour.
Traffic alarms should therefore be regarded as a supplementary tool rather than a primary safety measure, while sustainable improvements in road safety require continued emphasis on physical traffic‑calming measures, targeted enforcement, and interventions addressing the psychological mechanisms underlying risky driving behaviour.

projects.title: A Study of Reliability-Aware Super-Resolution in Robotic Laparoscopic Imaging
projects.abstract:
Super-resolution (SR) offers a promising solution
for enhancing laparoscopic imaging in minimal
invasive surgery, where cameras have limited
spatial resolution and low quality due hardware
constraints. However, improving resolution
alone does not guarantee reliable or clinically
trustworthy reconstructions, as SR may
hallucinate structures, and existing literature
focuses on image quality rather than reliability.
This thesis investigates how a deep learning–
based SR pipeline can enhance image quality
while explicitly modeling uncertainty and
ensuring reliability. A modular framework is
proposed, combining investigation of representative
SR models, such as EDSR and Swin2SR,
with reconstruction, uncertainty estimation and
reliability evaluation. Sensitivity-based uncertainty
maps are generated using perturbation
techniques, conformal prediction enables spatial
trust assessment through calibrated reliability
masks, and a conceptual unified reliability
score integrates fidelity, perceptual quality,
and uncertainty. Results show that Swin2SR
achieves superior performance, infer-transform
perturbation represents well uncertainty behavior,
and reliability varies spatially especially in
complex regions. The thesis demonstrates that
SR for medical imaging should be treated as a
reliability-aware imaging problem rather than
solely an image enhancement problem.

A Unified Security Assessment Framework for Hybrid Cryptographic Key Distribution Architectures
projects.abstract:
Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) is increasingly considered a promising approach for achieving long-term secure communication in the presence of future quantum-capable adversaries. However, QKD deployments rely not only on the quantum channel itself, but also on surrounding classical communication, authentication, synchronization, and key management. As a result, the overall security of hybrid QKD systems depends on some security assumptions that are often treated as trusted rather than validated.

This thesis proposes a structured security assessment framework for hybrid QKD-based key distribution architectures. The framework combines adversary models, security assumptions, practical validation, and a risk scoring model in order to see whether hybrid QKD deployments enforce their intended security guarantees. The framework doesn’t solely depend on theory, but it also requires running practical attacks on the infrastructure to evaluate it.

projects.title: Breathing Life into LCA: How Organisational Sensemaking Brings Environmental Impacts to Life
projects.abstract: Translating Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) results into meaningful and effective action in product development is challenging in practice. Although regulatory pressure and customer demands for environmental transparency are increasing, LCA often remains difficult for practitioners to interpret and apply in design decisions due to its complex and ambiguous nature. Using the electronics manufacturer DEIF A/S as a case, the study explores this challenge by combining a consequential cradle‑to‑grave LCA of DEIF’s iE 250 energy controller with ethnographic fieldwork, interviews, and a cross‑departmental workshop analysed through sensemaking theory. Sensemaking is employed to grasp the social and cognitive processes for interpreting and enacting LCA in the organisation. Use stage electricity consumption and the production of integrated circuits were identified as environmental hotspots. The organisational analysis reveals that such LCA results only influence product development when they are translated into formats and narratives that make sense. This process depends on negotiation, cross-departmental dialogue, and the presence of actors who bridge sustainability expertise and product development practices. The thesis concludes that successful integration of LCA is dependent on prioritising organisational sensemaking and interpretation rather than relying solely on raw LCA data to inform product development and decision-making. Strengthening interpretive and collaborative processes is therefore essential for translating environmental data into meaningful and actionable guidance for sustainable product development.

projects.title: Tracking household food waste beyond consumer-blame: A socio-technical response to the Danish household food waste measurement gap
projects.abstract:
Household food waste policies in Denmark and the EU currently rely on a fragile evidence base built on infrequent measurements, self-reported estimates, and top-down modelling. This structural measurement gap paralyzes effective governance. Rejecting the individualistic consumer-blame paradigm, this thesis reframes the household as a locked-in socio-technical site where waste is a structural byproduct of everyday routines and material arrangements. Using Practice Theory and the Multi-Level Perspective, the research combines systemic mapping, seven expert interviews, and a 19-household socio-technical photo-diary probe. It investigates how a materially embedded design intervention can simultaneously make waste physically visible to support domestic reduction, and function as a distributed infrastructure to generate the continuous, bottom-up primary data required to reform national policy.
Empirical findings reveal a mismatch between perceived and observed waste, confirming the structural distortions inherent in retrospective self-reporting. The data also demonstrates that household discard is heavily dictated by locked-in physical conditions, such as concealed bin placement and rigid retail formats. Aligning these observations with established research on the "measurement effect," the study argues that physical, point-of-disposal visibility must replace abstract awareness campaigns to effectively disrupt these routines. To successfully bridge the national measurement gap, a viable intervention must remain low-threshold to accommodate the distracted user, yet yield high-intensity, structured data aggregable at the macro-level. The thesis evaluates two dual-purpose design concepts: a material-centric smart scale and an infrastructure-centric AI-enabled bin, validated through expert and institutional feedback. Ultimately, neither concept seamlessly resolves the structural tension between frictionless domestic adoption and high-integrity data generation. The findings conclude that achieving accurate national metrics requires shifting measurement from a periodic administrative exercise to an everyday, physically integrated domestic routine.

From Board Room to Machine Room - Lost in translation? How Sustainability is Translated and Operationalised Through Tenders and Project Organisations
projects.abstract: Environmental sustainability is increasingly pursued through green procurement in infrastructure projects, yet challenges remain in translating sustainability ambitions into procurement practice. This study investigates how sustainability is shaped through tendering processes and how this influences actors within the project organisation. Drawing on Boundary Object In Sustainability Transitions (BOIST) framework, the tender is conceptualised as a boundary object through which sustainability is interpreted and operationalised. The study combines document analysis of tender material with semi-structured interviews with clients, consultants, and contractors. The findings suggest that sustainability emerges through competing organisational logics rather than procurement requirements alone. While ambitions, knowledge, and competencies are present across the project organisation, their influence remains fragmented across actors and organisational levels. The study concludes that challenges to sustainable procurement stem less from a lack of knowledge or ambition, and more from the difficulty of aligning sustainability-oriented logics within the project organisation.
