The behaviour of vulnerable road users in temporary traffic environments
projects.abstract:
This thesis investigates the behaviour of vulnerable road users around road work zones, with a particular focus on pedestrians and cyclists. The study examines how temporary traffic arrangements influence route choice, orientation, and perceived safety, as well as which factors contribute to non-compliant or potentially unsafe behaviour in complex traffic environments.

The research is based on a case study conducted at Stigsborg Brygge in Aalborg, Denmark, where extensive construction work and long-term temporary traffic management have created a complex environment for vulnerable road users. The analysis combines video observations, site inspections, and questionnaire surveys in order to examine both observed and perceived behaviour among pedestrians and cyclists travelling through the area.

The results indicate that the behaviour of vulnerable road users is highly influenced by how intuitive, coherent, and logical the temporary traffic environment is perceived to be. A considerable proportion of the observed road users did not follow the intended routes through the work zone, but instead selected alternative paths that were perceived as more direct or less cognitively demanding. This tendency was particularly evident among cyclists, many of whom avoided the designated turning facilities and instead travelled along unintended routes through the area.

Furthermore, the findings suggest that the physical layout of the work zone increased the cognitive workload of road users. The combination of temporary rerouting, barriers, parked vehicles, and varying traffic flows created a visually and cognitively demanding traffic environment. This appears to have contributed to delayed or insufficient orientation, as well as to several observed conflicts and non-compliant manoeuvres.

The thesis also indicates that vulnerable road users are influenced by habitual movement patterns and the behaviour of surrounding road users. Several observations showed that once one individual selected an alternative route, subsequent users followed the same path, thereby reinforcing traffic patterns within the work zone.

Based on the findings, the thesis concludes that temporary traffic arrangements for vulnerable road users should prioritise continuity, directness, visibility, and intuitive route guidance in order to support safe and compliant behaviour. The study further highlights the importance of integrating knowledge from traffic psychology and human factors into the planning and design of temporary traffic environments, as existing technical guidelines and minimum requirements may not alone be sufficient to ensure intuitive and safe traffic management in practice.

projects.title: From Visual to Functional Quality - Quality perceptions shaping remanufacturing at Grundfos
projects.abstract: This thesis addresses global challenges related to resource consumption, waste, and climate change, where a transition to circular economy (CE) is increasingly seen as necessary. Remanufacturing is a key circular strategy, yet its implementation remains challenging. At Grundfos, remanufactured components must appear visually “as new”, limiting the use of functionally suitable components. This study examines: How do quality perceptions at Grundfos shape the opportunities and barriers in changing the visual “as new” acceptance criteria for remanufactured components, to what extent can these perceptions be adapted, and what implications does this have for environmental and economic performance? The study applies a qualitative case study approach, with Grundfos as case, based on interviews, workshops, meetings, and participant observation, supported by scenario-based LCA calculations. The findings show that visual appearance acts as a proxy for quality, leading to the rejection of functional components. However, quality perceptions can be developed, enabling broader acceptance that increases component utilisation and reduces environmental impact with minor cost implications.

Achieving Digital Sovereignty Through Open Source: A Case Study of Enterprise Adoption of Open Source Infrastructure
projects.abstract: The emergence of digital sovereignty as a political priority in Europe has prompted organizations to explore open source software as a means of reducing dependency on American proprietary technology providers. This thesis investigates the technical, security, and organizational challenges that arise when an organization pursues digital sovereignty through open source adoption, and examines the extent to which open source solutions can satisfy enterprise compliance requirements. The research is conducted through a qualitative case study of Statens IT's SIA-Open initiative, a Danish public sector effort to establish an open source Linux-based workplace as an alternative to the existing Microsoft environment. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews with relevant stakeholders, supplemented by internal technical documentation. A proof of concept deployed Wazuh — selected through a structured evaluation of four candidate platforms using an extended five-criterion framework incorporating CWE profile analysis — as an open source EDR and SIEM solution across a hybrid Ubuntu, Windows, and macOS environment, evaluating it against De Tekniske Minimumskrav for Statslige Myndigheder. The evaluation demonstrated that an open source security stack can satisfy the baseline without dependency on foreign cloud infrastructure. However, open source adoption in a public sector context is further constrained by the absence of a national Open Source Program Office, a cost-recovery funding model, legacy system dependencies, and the paradox that coexistence with proprietary systems sustains the very dependencies the initiative seeks to reduce. Realizing the ambition of SIA-Open at scale requires stable funding, dedicated governance structures, and coordinated political commitment.

projects.title: Toward Gaze-Guided Prosthesis Preshaping: A Transferable Pipeline for Data-Driven Prosthesis Grasp Prediction and the Limits of Single-Frame Grasp Inference
projects.abstract:
Upper-limb prosthesis abandonment remains high, driven largely by control schemes that are slow and unintuitive.
Myoelectric control, which still dominates the field, struggles to deliver robust simultaneous control of multiple degrees of freedom, motivating shared-control systems that offload part of the intent inference onto user-agnostic sensing such as gaze.
This thesis presents a modular, label-free annotation pipeline that converts raw egocentric multimodal recordings into grasp-preshaping samples.
The pipeline detects gaze fixations on scene objects, detects and labels grasp events from hand--object contact, and links temporally disjoint fixations to the grasps they anticipate.
Applied to a 62-sequence subset of the HOT3D dataset, it produced 952 linked grasp events and 9982 fixation samples.
The annotations were evaluated along three axes.
A spatial analysis shows that anticipatory gaze lands on the functional grasp region for objects affording a distinct grip, but not for compact objects grasped over their whole body.
A module level quantitative and qualitative evaluation is performed, revealing high performance within the individual annotation submodules.
A downstream evaluation regresses MANO hand-pose principal components from a gaze-annotated 3D object mesh using graph neural networks; these models recover the dominant pose component (R² ≈ 0.15--0.20) where classical regressors fail entirely, but an ablation shows the gaze channel does not improve this prediction for any architecture.
Together these results indicate that the pipeline produces grasp data carrying genuine, geometry-grounded structure, while productively exploiting the anticipatory gaze signal will require integrating it beyond a per-vertex gaze feature.

projects.title: Automated ATT&CK Mapping and Adversary Classification in SSH Honeypot Sessions
projects.abstract:
Honeypots are commonly used to collect data about attacker activity, but the collected logs are often low-level and difficult to interpret manually. This project examines how attacker behaviour in SSH honeypot sessions can be analysed automatically by combining MITRE ATT&CK mapping with adversary classification.

The work follows a Design Science Research approach and is based on a deployed Cowrie honeypot, a live analysis pipeline, and a dashboard for structured session review. The system includes two classifiers. The first classifier maps individual shell commands to MITRE ATT&CK techniques using a retrieval and re-ranking approach built on ATT&CK data, Atomic Red Team examples, and command normalisation. The second classifier uses machine learning to categorise sessions as either human-driven or automated based on session-level behavioural features.

The results show that the proposed approach can support more structured analysis of SSH honeypot data. At the same time, the project also highlights several limitations, including the use of heuristic labels, limited command context, dataset size, and the ambiguity of some commands.

projects.title: Contesting Epistemic Colonialism Through Grassroots Techno-pedagogy in Latin America: Decolonial Perspectives from Colombia
projects.abstract:
Despite the growing decolonial turn in contemporary debates, knowledge production, circulation and validation in Latin America remains shaped by enduring forms of coloniality that privilege Eurocentric knowledge systems while marginalizing local, Indigenous, and community-based ways of knowing. Although decolonial discourse offers insightful ways to identify and map manifestations of epistemic colonialism in the region, it lacks concrete methodological and analytical tools to effectively examine and guide decolonial commitments in practice, particularly when enacted outside formal institutions. This thesis argues that grassroots initiatives should take up more space in decolonial scholarship and moves on to address this gap by investigating whether and how grassroots techno-pedagogy can contest epistemic colonialism and enable alternative forms of knowledge production in Latin American contexts.
Drawing on the concept of pluriverse, grassroots social innovation, and a reconceptualization of techno-pedagogy as a form of decolonial praxis, the thesis develops an original four-dimensional analytical framework consisting of epistemic, ontological, organizational, and pedagogical dimensions. The framework is applied to an illustrative case study of DakotaLab, a grassroots initiative grounded in techno-pedagogical practices, operating in the rural region of Meta, in Colombia. The empirical analysis draws on ethnographically informed multi-sited fieldwork, semi-structured interviews, participant observation, document analysis, and participatory design activities with students, educators, and community actors across rural and urban settings.
The findings suggest that grassroots techno-pedagogy can contribute to contesting epistemic colonialism by fostering community-oriented, territorially embedded, and pluralistic forms of knowledge production. DakotaLab’s practices reveal that grassroots can be understood as sites of decolonial flourishing, although not in a definitive or complete way, by creating spaces in which local knowledges, alternative sociotechnical imaginaries, and critical engagements with technology can emerge and gain legitimacy. At the same time, the analysis reveals important tensions between decolonial aspirations and the structural constraints within which grassroots
initiatives operate, demonstrating both the possibilities and limitations of grassroots decolonial praxis and highlighting the value of examining them as sites of epistemic resistance. The thesis contributes to decolonial scholarship by providing a novel analytical framework to investigate and guide decolonial commitments, by extending the focus of the current decolonial approaches beyond formal institutions, and by advancing grassroots techno-pedagogy as a decolonial praxis that can contest epistemic colonialism and enable alternative forms of knowledge production in Latin American contexts.

projects.title: Coastal Adaptation
projects.abstract:
Dette studie undersøger, hvordan kommunalt skøn ved bidragsfordeling efter kystbeskyttelseslovens §9a kan bidrage til at forklare implementeringsudfordringer i kystbeskyttelsesprojekter. Problemfeltet tager afsæt i, at bidragsfordeling ikke kun handler om finansiering, men også om hvordan kommuner omsætter vurderinger af nytte til konkrete betalingsforpligtelser for berørte grundejere.
Studiet besvarer problemformuleringen gennem en kvalitativ tilgang. Juridisk metode er anvendt til at klarlægge rammerne for kommunalt skøn under §9a, mens et casestudie af dige projekterne i Bogense og Høll undersøger, hvordan skønnet anvendes i konkrete bidragsmodeller på baggrund af kommunale dokumenter og klagesager. Interviews med aktører, der har erfaring fra arbejdet med bidragsfordelingsmodeller, er inkluderet for at belyse praksisnære perspektiver, som ikke fremgår direkte af dokumentmaterialet.
Konklusionen på studiet er, at §9a giver kommunerne et nødvendigt, men konflikt følsomt handlerum. Implementeringsudfordringer opstår især, når juridisk gyldige nyttevurderinger omsættes til økonomiske bidrag, som berørte grundejere ikke nødvendigvis oplever som forståelige eller retfærdige. Derfor kræver en velfungerende bidragsfordeling ikke kun et lovligt fordelingsgrundlag, men også klare kriterier, tydelig begrundelse og en proces, hvor berørte grundejere oplever, at deres indsigelser bliver taget alvorligt.

TapResult: A columnar file format with an evolving schema
projects.abstract: This report builds on the work of our report from the previous semester, where we established what requirements are necessary for a good file format for OpenTAP. We examine a few file formats to use as an example, and draw inspiration from different parts of the formats. Then we go into detail about the design of a new file format, called TapResult. Next we describe the current applications of TapResult in the form of a CLI tool and a plugin for OpenTAP. Then we move on to describe our experiments, both on write, read and compression, and what was learnt from these experiments. Here we also introduce two complementary file formats for TapResult, called TapData/TapSchema, that build upon the same ideas as TapResult. Finally we discuss the results of the report and what could be done in the future of this file format.

projects.title: Sustainability Integration Framework: Addressing the Sustainability Implementation Gap
projects.abstract:
This study examines how corporate sustainability strategies are
managed, validated, and translated into practice within a large
organization, based on a case study conducted in collaboration with
Copenhagen Airports A/S. Drawing on Staging Negotiation Spaces and
Arena of Development, the research explores how sustainability
strategies are operationalized in this specific organizational context.
The findings indicate a limited implementation of sustainability within
existing project structures, where it remains weakly integrated into
processes of prioritization and execution. Governance practices are
predominantly shaped by established organizational value logics, within
which sustainability must be translated to gain traction. Furthermore,
implementation emerges as contingent on informal coordination, rather
than being supported by cross-collaboration, formalized structures, and
clearly defined responsibilities.

As part of this work, the Sustainability Integration Framework (SIF) is
designed to address how strategies can be effectively implemented and
translated into practice, particularly within the CPH Project Model.

Circular Communities in Holbæk Municipality
projects.abstract:
This thesis aims to contribute with research on how the social dimension of circular economy can be manifested in practice by examining the dynamics between local authorities and local communities working with activities related to waste prevention and reuse, as these aspects of circular economy are currently lacking in a Danish context. The thesis will use Holbæk Municipality as the case, with a focus on three local circular communities.

This thesis examines how Holbæk Municipality and Fors can strengthen their collaboration with local circular communities to support a local transition towards circular economy. This study will take a point of departure in the following research question: How can local authorities strengthen their collaboration with circular communities in Holbæk Municipality to support a local transition towards circular economy?

First, three circular communities are analysed using the theory of Transformative Social Innovation as an analytical framework to understand their relations and their potential to become transformative. Second, the theory of Multi-Level Perspective is used as the analytical framework to analyse the current regime, the lock-in mechanisms for a local transition towards circular economy, as well as the possible windows of opportunity for this transition. This leads to a discussion of the relevance of rethinking the roles of the local authorities to support circular communities, and how this can be mutually beneficial.

It is concluded that local authorities can be more proactive and supportive, when involving and mobilising circular communities, even though they experience regime constraints. This expanded role will benefit both the local authorities and the circular communities, as the local authorities aim to increase their focus on waste prevention and reuse rather than recycling alone and involve citizens in this agenda. Meanwhile, the circular communities need resources, legitimacy and network to be stabilised and realise their transformative potential. In this transition, local authorities should be aware not to take over the circular communities or their ideas, while the communities should not become too embedded in the existing nstitutions, as it may constrain their transformative potential.

projects.title: Otoacoustic Emissions - Investigation of Multiple Frequency Distortion Product Otoacoustic Emissions
projects.abstract:
This thesis investigates the topic of Multi Frequency Distortion Product Otoacoustic Emissions (MF-DPOAE), aiming to improve measurement speed of DPOAEs by concurrently stimulating primaries (f1,f2) and measuring multiple distortion prodcts (2f1-f2). This is achieved without adding significant bias the measured SNR, DP levels, and noise floor.

A MATLAB-based MF-DPOAE algorithm was developed and implemented on the Interacoustics Titan, incorporating multi-tone stimulus generation, calibration, noise estimation, and spectral leakage mitigation. Three frequency pairing strategies were evaluated: octave-based and two algorithm-based approaches.

Results show that MF-DPOAE provides comparable performance to standard DPOAE in six-frequency configurations with reduced measurement time. However, twelve-frequency configurations exhibit increased variability and noise. 

These findings indicate MF-DPOAE is a viable solution for faster measurements when frequency selection and noise estimation are carefully managed. Future work should focus on refining noise estimation, optimizing adaptive frequency scheduling, and validating on larger populations.
keywords: Multiple Frequency Distortion Product Otoacoustic Emissions

Design and Verification of a Fault Injection Module for White Rabbit Networks
projects.abstract: White Rabbit is a high-accuracy synchronization protocol built on Ethernet and IEEE 1588, capable of achieving sub-nanosecond timing accuracy. As its adoption grows in critical infrastructure, verifying resilience against physical layer faults becomes increasingly important, yet no dedicated fault injection tooling exists for White Rabbit systems. This report presents the design and implementation of a VHDL fault injection module, integrated into the White Rabbit PTP Core, supporting multiple categories of physical layer errors spanning data corruption, symbol manipulation, and \acs{ddmtd} phase disturbances. The module exposes its control interface through Wishbone-mapped registers, accessible from both simulations and through a command-line tool on real hardware. The implemented module is functionally verified in simulation and partially validated on physical White Rabbit hardware, where eight of ten modes produced observable hardware effects, one caused unexpected PTP failure at low injection rates, and two timing modes remain un-validated due to a SoftPLL lock issue.

projects.title: Urban Refuge - An approach to reimagining Bispeengbuen as a multispecies zone
projects.abstract: Urban biodiversity has become an increasingly important planning concern as cities expand while biodiversity continues to decline globally. Although biodiversity strategies and assessment tools are becoming more widespread, challenges remain regarding how biodiversity ambitions are translated into actionable planning and design practices. Using the planned reopening of Ladegårdsåen and the transformation of Bispeengbuen in Copenhagen as a case study, this project investigates how biodiversity data, biodiversity strategies, and stakeholder knowledge can be translated into actionable design parameters through biodiversity assessment tools. Drawing on Actor-Network Theory, Multispecies Design, and UrbanBioScore, the project analyses the actor-network surrounding urban biodiversity implementation in Copenhagen. The findings reveal fragmented responsibilities and implementation barriers across sectors, while highlighting how NGOs, private consultancies, and biodiversity assessment tools contribute to mobilising ecological concerns within urban planning processes. Based on these findings, the project develops Refugia, a biodiversity design guide that translates biodiversity assessments into ecological and anthropological design parameters. The project argues that biodiversity assessment tools can support urban biodiversity beyond measurement alone when combined with design-oriented translation mechanisms. In doing so, it proposes a shift from biodiversity assessment as result towards biodiversity assessment as recipe, demonstrating how Sustainable Design Engineering can support the operationalisation of biodiversity within complex urban planning networks.

projects.title: Prior Anchored Continuous-Time Trajectory Anomaly Detection
projects.abstract: Trajectory anomaly detection in large-scale road networks is severely hindered by extreme data sparsity and the reliance on discrete temporal representations. Existing graph-based methods struggle to scale beyond localized urban subgraphs and often neglect temporal dynamics, while the scarcity of labeled real-world anomalies limits rigorous evaluation. We propose Prior-Anchored Continuous-Time Trajectory Anomaly Detection (PACT-TAD), a framework that addresses these challenges through three tightly integrated contributions. First, we introduce a topology-aware Bayesian Graph Attention Network prior that anchors travel time estimation to free-flow travel times while modeling temporal dynamics continuously via harmonic functions, enabling robust inference on unobserved road segments. Second, we develop a procedural anomaly generation engine that produces physically plausible spatial, temporal, and compound spatio-temporal anomalies by combining stochastic routing with autoregressive temporal processes. Third, we present a scalable dual-head sequence architecture based on a Bidirectional GRU that performs fine-grained edge-level anomaly detection, regularized by supervised contrastive learning on known anomaly subtypes. Extensive experiments on the Danish national road network, consisting of 1.4 million edges, demonstrate that PACT-TAD significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both spatial and temporal anomaly detection while scaling successfully where comparative methods fail due to memory or computational constraints. The framework achieves strong performance under data sparsity and contributes a rigorous synthetic benchmark through its physically constrained anomaly generation engine.

projects.title: Algorithmic Decision-Support Systems for Expropriation Compensation
projects.abstract:
This master’s thesis examines the possibility of using Algorithmic Decision Systems (ADS) to support decision-making regarding expropriation compensation. Specifically, the thesis focuses on the assessment of compensation for injurious affection in expropriation decisions. This is especially relevant because the Danish administrative instrument of expropriation is contentious, and the use of ADS in general is becoming more widespread. Furthermore, the compensation for injurious affection is discretionary and often based on intuitive judgment, which leads to an interesting tension between discretionary practice and more advanced data-driven technologies like Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Machine Learning (ML). Therefore, the following research question is investigated:

To what extent can patterns be identified in the assessment of compensation for injurious affection in expropriation decisions through Natural Language Processing, and what indications do such patterns provide for the development of a usable Algorithmic Decision System?

This research question is answered based on a critical rationalist approach, where theories and existing knowledge in relation to Algorithmic Decision Systems (ADS), including Legal Judgement Prediction (LJP), NLP and ML, are applied to the expropriation domain. To identify the most relevant literature and theories, the study uses a systematic literature search method supplemented by expert interviews. Furthermore, an NLP pipeline is constructed based on the literature identified, with the intent of identifying patterns in the discretionary practice regarding the determination of compensation for injurious affection. Three different NLP techniques are utilised: TF-IDF, Doc2Vec, and LDA. Expert interviews are used to synthesise and discuss the findings from the different NLP analyses and to provide insight into the discretionary practice.

Through the different analyses, it was found that NLP can identify patterns in issued decisions on compensation for injurious affection in expropriation cases. However, when using these patterns as features in an XGBoost ML model, with the intent of predicting the compensation for injurious affection, the result is an R2 value of 0.25. This suggests that the model is merely able to explain 25 percent of the injurious affection compensation variance. Thus, it is concluded that the patterns found by NLP techniques only provide limited explanatory power regarding the determination of the amount of compensation. Therefore, the patterns are more valuable as a basis for systematizing practice and identifying comparable decisions for use as decision support, and not as a basis for a fully automated compensation determination tool. Herby, the analysis indicates that it is possible to construct simple and interpretable ADS, but more complex predictive ML-systems can be restricted in both accuracy and transparency.

projects.title: Centralised Collaborative SLAM in the Lunar Environment
projects.abstract:
This project presents the design and implementa-
tion of a Centralised Collaborative Simultaneous
Localisation and Mapping (CSLAM) system for
two or more rovers operating on the lunar sur-
face. The primary environmental challenges ad-
dressed are the sparse visual texture of lunar re-
golith and extreme high-contrast lighting, both of
which impede standard vision-based localisation.
To overcome these, LiDAR is used alongside an
RGBD camera and IMU, with RTAB-Map as the
core SLAM and map-merging framework. The
system follows a centralised architecture in which
each rover performs local SLAM and periodically
transfers its map database to a base station, which
merges all maps into a unified global representa-
tion and redistributes it to the fleet.
The system was developed in ROS2 Humble,
containerised with Docker, and was first imple-
mented in an Isaac Sim lunar-analogue simula-
tion before physical testing on the AAU Space
Robotics rover Gorm at Aalborg Portland Rørdal
limestone quarry. Hardware modifications to
Gorm, including a soft motor starter, USB hub,
and Ethernet switch, were required to integrate
the new sensor suite. Field tests confirmed the
system’s ability to perform per-robot SLAM and
merge maps from multiple rovers into a single co-
herent map.

Shared Software Radio Unit for NTN NB-IoT Systems
projects.abstract:
Narrowband Internet of Things (NB-IoT) has migrated from a Long Term Evolution (LTE) enhancement into a technology integrated with 5th Generation (5G). This thesis investigates a system that combines three individually established approaches, a split 8 functional split, a bent-pipe NTN deployment, and a shared Open Radio Access Network (ORAN) Radio Unit (O-RU) serving multiple O-RAN Distributed Units (O-DUs). The proposed O-RU performs frequency shifting and combination of multiple O-DUs' NB-IoT carriers into a single wideband feeder-link signal in the time domain at split 8.

A user-plane architecture for this shared O-RU is designed. The design is realized as a software O-RU and evaluated using a testbed. Validation testing confirms that the composite wideband signal is correctly formed and that each carrier can be cleanly recovered. A performance test then characterizes the maximum number of concurrently serviceable carriers as a function of worker cores, for upsampling factors of 2 and 4. At an upsampling factor of 2 the system is spectrally limited to 14 carriers regardless of core count, whereas at an upsampling factor of 4 it becomes computationally limited, supporting 10, 16, 21, 24, and 24 carriers for one through five worker cores respectively.

projects.title: Time Division Duplexing in 3GPP based Non-Terrestrial Networks
projects.abstract: With the developments towards 6G, the interest in using TDD for LEO NTN has re-emerged. The efficiency of TDD is constrained by the prolonged propagation delays in NTNs, which increases GP durations in order to avoid self-interference, causing increased latency. This work designs and proposes two solutions: (1) A Cluster-based solution which allows concurrent UL and DL transmissions, by requiring a minimum UE-to-UE distance resulting in negligible CLI. (2) A SRP based solution where the long propagation delays are leveraged for synchronous UL and DL transmissions that are fully contained within the simultaneous propagation duration. Using a system level simulation, the proposed solutions are evaluated against a naive Baseline solution for two traffic scenarios. The proposed solutions both reduce latency across all metrics, with the Cluster-based solution decreasing the 95th percentile UL latency by 21% and the SRP solution decreasing the 95th percentile DL latency by 65%

projects.title: Building New Pathways: A study on Staging Negotiation Spaces for Sustainable Business Development in the Construction Sector
projects.abstract:
With the built environment being one of the sectors responsible for the largest share of global emissions and resource consumption, circular economy is cemented as the political and economic agenda towards sustainable transition of the construction industry. Remanufacturing offers a circular strategy to material value retention, which through circular business model innovation enables pathways for practitioners to implement remanufactured components within construction- However, the adoption of circular solutions in building projects encounters barriers, as stakeholders and practitioners of the construction industry share concerns towards circular building products. Additionally, limited research examines how these concerns can be strategically addressed by the manufacturers, to promote the transition.

The present study investigates the stakeholder concerns from the perspective of a Danish remanufacturing company, with the application of the Arena of Development and Staging Negotiation Spaces frameworks. The study explores the concerns of developers, architects, engineers and contractors, to define the tensions inhibiting the adoption of circular building products and conceptualizes scenarios for further design. Through the participatory design approach and based on analysis of stakeholder concerns and prioritizations, the study concludes how remanufacturers can strategically address the concerns of contractors to increase conversion and adoption of circular solutions in the construction industry. Consequently, the study contributes to the research of barriers and drivers to accelerate circular economy in the construction sector by uncovering the underlying stakeholder concerns and providing a context-specific design approach to negotiating concepts for further collaboration.

projects.title: Extending the Load Balancing for Cadence
projects.abstract:
This report is a 10th-semester com-
puter science project for AAU, con-
ducted in collaboration with Uber.
Building on our prior work, we design
and evaluate three extensions in the
Cadence open-source codebase: sup-
port for heterogeneous Matching ex-
ecutors, swap moves for balanced two-
shard exchanges, and cost-aware scor-
ing to limit disruptive shard moves.
The evaluation combines algorithm re-
play with a Kubernetes testbed on pro-
duction traces.
Under increasing load, latency-aware
balancing completes 105% more work-
flows than the previous contribution
and 80% more than CPU-time aware
correction. Cost-aware scoring reduces
moved shard load by 25% when added
to latency-aware balancing, at a cost of
a 7.5% reduction in completed work-
flows. Swap moves only marginally
impacted the results in Uber’s produc-
tion load traces.

projects.title: Sustainable healthcare: Transitioning from disposable to reusable suture kits in Region Hovedstaden
projects.abstract:
This master thesis investigates how Region Hovedstaden can transition from disposable suture kits to reusable alternatives as part of its ambition to meet the organization’s 2030 sustainability goal and advance sustainable healthcare practices. The study is conducted as a case study, focusing on the Emergency Department Bispebjerg and examines the operational and logistical, challenges of replacing disposable suture kits with reusable suture kits. It answers the following research questions:
How can Region Hovedstaden phase out the use of disposable suture kits to reuseable alternatives to meet their 2030 sustainability goal and to support sustainable healthcare?
Through a mapping of the life cycle of disposable suture kits, the thesis identifies environmental hotspot through the life cycle and analyses the cost of reusable suture kits. It also identifies the main barriers and opportunities that influence the feasibility of implementation, including knowledge gaps, logistical and behavioral practices. The analysis explores the potential costs and benefits associated with reusable suture kits, assessing both economic and environmental dimensions. Together, these insights contribute to understanding how Region Hovedstaden can effectively phase out disposable suture kits and support a broader transition toward sustainable healthcare.

projects.title: Automatic parameter calibration method for SHM feature generation schemes
DIGITAL INCLUSION AS A MEDIATED PROCESS: A PARTICIPATORY STUDY OF DIGITAL LEARNING SUPPORT WITHIN FINKLUSIV'S DIGITAL BRIDGE BUILDERS' INITIATIVE
projects.abstract: In an increasingly digital world, businesspeople are expected to engage with online platforms, administrative systems and digital communication tools during their business activities. The processes can be difficult for entrepreneurs with migrant and refugee backgrounds because of language barriers, different institutional systems, and different levels of experience with digital. Digital inclusion is mostly talked about in terms of access to technology and digital skills, but less in relation to the development of learning support to enable people to engage with these systems in practice. The thesis examines the development of digital learning support in the Digital Bridge Builders project in Finklusiv, which works with underbanked entrepreneurs with a migrant or refugee background in Denmark. It has a focus on the volunteer training phase during which volunteers are introduced to digital tools, learning materials and support practices which are designed to help entrepreneurs navigate digital systems. From a techno-anthropological point of view, in which postphenomenology as an epistemological framework is applied, the study analyses how the digital learning support is created during the interaction of technologies, learning materials, volunteers and workshops. The empirical material comprises video resources, webpages, presentation materials, transcriptions and workshop observations. The results reveal that digital inclusion is not just about technology and technical skills. There was an emphasis on the need for communication, trust, language and understanding of institutional systems in the workshop discussions. Meaningful digital participation is theorized to emerge through context-sensitive learning support and collaborative engagement and is seen as part of a broader process of digital inclusion, influenced by technologies, social interaction and learning practices.
keywords: Digital Inclusion, Technological Mediation, Postphenomenology, Participatory Learning, Entrepreneurial Support, Digital Participation

projects.title: A Simulation-Based Observation Planning Tool for the Máni Lunar Orbiter under Pointing Uncertainty
projects.abstract: The Máni mission is a European Space Agency (ESA) lunar orbiter that will map the surface of the Moon using multi-angular photoclinometric imaging. Unlike conventional mapping missions, which acquire a single image of each target, Máni must acquire at least five overlapping images of every surface target across a wide range of observation angles, repeated over two overflights separated by roughly one lunar sidereal period to capture distinct illumination conditions. Whether a candidate orbit can satisfy this requirement depends on the interaction between the orbital parameters, which fix the available viewing geometry, and the spacecraft pointing uncertainty, which displaces each image footprint from its intended position on the surface. This interaction is currently unquantified for Máni, and existing orbit analysis and pointing error tools address the two factors only in isolation. We design and implement a simulation module that takes a candidate orbit configuration, derives the observation geometry over a region of interest, schedules image acquisitions through an exchangeable scheduler, and uses Monte Carlo simulation to estimate the probability that the five-image overlap requirement is met under a configurable pointing error model. We exercise the module across a range of orbital configurations, region layouts, error models, and scheduling assumptions. The results suggest that it responds meaningfully to its inputs: it distinguishes orbits with equal overlap but different angular diversity, exposes how target spacing and the number of overflights govern region completion, and, by reporting coverage as a distribution rather than a single value, makes worst-case outcomes visible to mission planners.

projects.title: RF Cavity Hardware Simulator for the HL-LHC at CERN
projects.abstract:
ow-level RF control systems for the
HL-LHC require accurate simulation
and validation tools to enable early prototyping and testing of feedback controllers. Although electrical models of
the cavity exist, implemented hardware
simulations that capture latency, frequency response, and measurement uncertainties remain unavailable.
This report describes the design steps, implementation and validation of an FPGA-based cavity hardware simulator. A key
technical challenge is to develop a digital filter in baseband, with frequency
detuning capability, while reducing resource usage and latency.
Each implementation stage, from
continuous-time model through
discrete-time and RTL simulation to
hardware, was validated against the
preceding stage. The simulator achieves
the required latency and frequency coverage for the target application, demonstrates frequency detuning, and produces the desired frequency response.

projects.title: Probabilistic design for wind turbine load assessment
Cold-water coral ecosystems in Danish and adjacent waters: knowledge recovery, ecological resilience, and future conservation strategies
projects.abstract: Cold-water corals are present in Danish and adjacent Scandinavian waters, but knowledge about their distribution, conservation relevance and restoration potential remains fragmented. This thesis investigates how knowledge of cold-water coral ecosystems can be recovered, structured and translated into future conservation and restoration strategies that support marine ecosystem resilience.Using a qualitative case study approach, the research combines document-based research, study visits, observations and semi-structured interviews. The findings show that Alcyonium digitatum is present in Danish waters but remains poorly mapped and less visible in conservation discussions, while Lophelia pertusa has stronger restoration relevance in Sweden and Norway. Based on socio-ecological systems and resilience theory, the thesis develops an exploratory decision-making framework for future conservation pathways, showing that cold-water coral strategies should begin with knowledge recovery, monitoring and species-specific assessment before active restoration is considered.

projects.title: Vurdering og optimering af \\indeklima og installationer i \\en eksisterende kontorbygning
Digital Support for Women During ADHD Medication Initiation for Clinical Dialogue
Playful track and field training - the impact on childrens motivation and engagement
projects.abstract:
Purpose: This study investigates how a playful approach to track and field training promotes motivation and engagement in children aged 9-11 in an athletics club.
Methods: The theoretical framework is grounded in Basic Psychological Needs Theory (BPNT) and Organismic Integration Theory (OIT) (Deci & Ryan, 2017), alongside engagement theory (Fredericks et al. 2004). Methodologically, the study adopts a pragmatic research stance and employs Design Thinking as an iterative framework in the development, trial and adjustment of the playful training activities. In addition, the didactical tools lege-mixerpulten and lege-pendulet were used to structure and adjust the playful activities. The empirical foundation comprises participant observations from six training sessions, three workshops with coaches, two focus group interviews with the children, and questionnaire data (BRSQ‑6; PNSS‑S). This mixed‑methods design enables methodological triangulation and a comprehensive understanding of motivational and engagement‑related processes. Results: The qualitative analysis identified four central factors influencing children's engagement in playful track and field training: variation and randomness; opportunities for autonomy; the framing of activities and social relationships. Engagement varied across activities and participants and was expressed through behavioural, emotional, and cognitive dimensions. Playful elements such as unpredictability, role-play, and opportunities for experimentation appeared to support engagement, while unclear task understanding and overly demanding or insufficiently challenging activities could reduce engagement. The quantitative findings indicated positive developments in perceived autonomy, competence, and relatedness across the intervention, alongside a shift towards a more self-determined type of motivation. A statistically significant increase was observed in children's perceived competence in athletics (p = 0.044).
Conclusion: The findings indicate that a playful approach to track and field training has the potential to contribute to supporting children's motivation and engagement. While the quantitative results showed limited statistically significant changes beyond perceived competence, the qualitative findings suggest that a playful approach can create conditions that support engagement through variation, autonomy, framing of activities and social relationships.

projects.title: Encountering the Court: The Witness in the Criminal Justice Process
projects.abstract:
This thesis examines how witnesses experience the institutional processes of the Danish criminal justice system when encountering it for the first time, and how this encounter shapes their orientation towards the legal system and their perception of its legitimacy.
The study is based on qualitative interviews with six witnesses and ten professionals, including legal actors and the support and service functions that work with the target group. Drawing on both current legislation and perspectives from practice, the first part of the analysis outlines the criminal procedure to which witnesses are subjected, from the receipt of the summons through the court hearing and into the period afterwards. The second part of the analysis examines the witnesses' own experiences across four phases that emerge from the empirical material: the summons, the waiting period, the court hearing, and the aftermath.
The mapping of the procedure reveals a legal process containing numerous points of attention, which makes it understandable that some witnesses find it difficult to comprehend and navigate a process that they are suddenly obliged to take part in. The analysis of the witnesses' experiences finds that, while accounts vary, a majority share a sense of not possessing the knowledge of the system or the information needed to find peace of mind before the hearing. This sense is confirmed throughout the process, where unforeseen elements create discomforting situations in the encounter with the courts, including intimidating meetings with the defendant and questioning by defence counsel that destabilises the witness's sense of their own role. Positive experiences also occur, particularly in the meeting with service functions and in courtrooms that feel less formal than expected, but across these differences the witnesses share a retrospective wish to have been better prepared.
The thesis argues that attention to the witness as an actor in their own right, regardless of any additional role, is essential for ensuring support, safety and the continued legitimacy of the system.
The thesis concludes with a set of recommendations for practice drawn from the witnesses' experiences and from the tensions between these and the perspectives of legal actors.

projects.title: Using Physical Modeling, Machine Learning, and Virtual Reality for Replicating the Ancient Greek Lyre
projects.abstract: This thesis investigates an end-to-end system for turning audio recordings of a musical instrument into an interactable, performable digital twin, motivated by the difficulty museums face in conveying the sound of instruments too fragile or rare to be handled. Developed around the ancient Greek lyre, using recordings gifted by the Seikilo Museum of Ancient Music, the system combines a body impulse-response extractor, a machine-learning optimizer that uses differentiable digital signal processing to estimate physical model parameters from audio, and a virtual-reality tool in which the resulting instruments are played. Each is evaluated objectively and perceptually. The impulse-response extractor reproduces a target body convincingly; the parameter optimizer struggles to recover consistent, physically meaningful values but shows promise on a problem with little prior work; and the virtual-reality tool reaches the usability benchmark for an average system, with its sound being a clear strength. Together the results establish a workable foundation for bringing historical instruments into an interactive digital form.

projects.title: Bayesian Modelling of Recruitment Dynamics in Multi-Site Clinical Trials: Interim Recruitment Prediction in Cardiovascular Outcomes Trials Using Poisson-Gamma Models
projects.abstract:
This thesis develops and evaluates a Bayesian
hierarchical framework for modelling site-level
recruitment dynamics, applied to four completed Novo Nordisk A/S sponsored cardiovascular outcomes trials.
Six nested Poisson-Gamma models of increasing complexity are specified. The models incorporate a COVID-19 effect, a shared exponential decay in recruitment intensity over
relative site opening days, weekend effects, a
site-level planned patient goal covariate, and
regional effects. Parameters are estimated using Markov Chain Monte Carlo via JAGS.
Predictive performance is evaluated at sequential interim time points using bias and interval
width of posterior predictive intervals of accumulated recruitments and predicted trial
completion day.
The homogeneous model is consistently the
worst performer across all trials, confirming
that a constant site-level recruitment intensity
is too restrictive. The remaining five models
perform comparably, and no clear ranking
among them is established, due to varying
results across models and trials, as well as a
systematic sampling error in the prediction
procedure that underestimates the number of
open sites.
A key challenge across all models, except the
homogeneous model, is the reliable estimation
of the exponential decay parameter at early
interim time points due to limited data on
the full trajectory of site-level recruitment.
To accommodate this, a cross-trial prediction
approach using moment-matched informative
priors derived from completed trials is suggested, which shows predictive performance
improves when source trials have similar dynamics, but also reveals sensitivity to prior
specification.

projects.title: Assessing the Role of Solar Parks as Biodiversity Refugia in Agricultural Landscapes
projects.abstract:
The rapid expansion of utility-scale solar parks
has raised concerns regarding their impacts on
biodiversity. However, solar parks may also pro-
vide opportunities for ecological restoration by
reducing agricultural disturbance and promot-
ing habitat heterogeneity. This study evaluated
the potential of solar parks to function as biodi-
versity refugia within agricultural landscapes us-
ing soil environmental DNA (eDNA). The solar
park differed from the agricultural field in both
environmental conditions and biodiversity pat-
terns, suggesting that changes in management,
vegetation cover and soil conditions have al-
ready influenced community assembly. Commu-
nity analyses indicated that the solar park sup-
ported taxa associated with semi-natural habi-
tats while simultaneously retaining elements of
its former agricultural community. The results
suggest that the solar park displayed charac-
teristics intermediate between agricultural fields
and freshwater meadows, supporting its poten-
tial role as a transitional habitat and biodiversity
refugium. However, responses differed among
taxonomic groups, highlighting the complexity
of biodiversity responses and the need for long-
term studies to evaluate the ecological influence
of solar park development.

projects.title: System Capability for Sustainability Reporting in an Inland Freight Coordination Company
projects.abstract:
This master’s thesis investigates system capability for CSRD-aligned sustainability reporting in a Finnish inland freight coordination company. The aim is to gain understanding of how sustainability data can be collected and reported. Additionally, it is examined how a baseline can be drawn for emissions generated by so-called empty drives, where a truck is driving without cargo, and how these could be mitigated.
During the project period the software system used by the case company was studied in detail. The focus was on the system’s capabilities as well as the way it was being used by the company. Autoethnographic observation while working in the company yielded valuable insights into attitudes and working practices in the company as well as deeper understanding of the platform’s use cases, features, and limitations. As a result, the transport management system can produce CSRD compliant emission data. A system solution was found for promoting circular route planning. Additionally, several concrete suggestions for enhanced system utilization were cultivated.
Based on the insights gained through this thesis project, it can be stated that there is substantial room for improvement in the system utilization within the company. The most relevant sustainability data for reporting consists of delivery distances, cargo weight, and equipment fuel consumption. This data can be extracted from the system and formatted into reports. In its current state, the system can track circular deliveries, but adjustments need to be made to the way data is logged. The system can process significantly more information than it is currently being used for. By taking full advantage of the system’s features, its strategic value increases in the future.
keywords: logistics, transport, transportation, freight logistics coordination, sea freight, container, sustainability reporting, CSRD, sustainable logistics, emission

projects.title: ClinicalQA: A benchmark for end-to-end evaluation of QA systems over JSON documents
projects.abstract:
Modern Question Answering (QA) systems struggle to accurately process complex, semi-structured data like JSON. Current benchmarks fail to expose these vulnerabilities because they do not focus on how structural complexity affects performance and they isolate information retrieval (IR) from answer generation (AG). To accurately measure real-world, end-to-end performance, we introduce ClinicalQA, a novel benchmark composed of structurally complex JSON documents. Using this benchmark alongside existing datasets, we evaluate two primary paradigms: a state-of-the-art Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline, Magikarp, and a Natural Language to Query Language architecture, NL2JQ. Our findings
reveal that ClinicalQA effectively measures both the IR and AG capabilities of Magikarp. Conversely, we find that NL2JQ fundamentally lacks the capacity for document retrieval and free-text answer generation, rendering it incompatible with ClinicalQA. Furthermore, our analysis demonstrates how early retrieval failures systematically cascade into downstream generation errors, highlighting the fundamental necessity of enabling end-to-end evaluation of QA systems. Finally, the results reveal that both the IR and AG performance of these systems are directly affected by the structural complexity of the ground-truth JSON context, specifically its average leaf depth and branching factor.

projects.title: Price Prediciton - How Much Data Do You Need?
projects.abstract:
Short-term electricity price forecasting is critical for
industrial energy planning and grid stability. However, existing
literature often focuses on computationally expensive, highly
specialised architectures tested on fixed
feature sets. This leaves industry practitioners without clear guidance
regarding whether the acquisition of diverse feature sets and increased model
complexity is justified. This thesis presents a large-scale ablation study of
the Danish
day-ahead
electricity market, systematically evaluating 1,052 default-configured
machine
learning models across eight architectures.
These include tree-based models, neural networks, and an automatic machine
learning ensemble framework by the name of AutoGluon.
The models are assessed using walk-forward validation across 13
progressively expanding feature constellations, eight forecasting
horizons, ranging from 0-hours to 168-hours, and two prediction
targets: absolute price and price difference.
Results demonstrate that, under default
configurations, general-purpose tree-based
models, particularly CatBoost, outperform neural
network architectures at short-term forecasting
horizons. Feature contribution analysis reveals
that historical price data is the most critical predictive feature,
whereas expanding the dataset to include lagged grid consumption
metrics yields diminishing or negative returns. Supplementary
experiments demonstrate that targeted hyperparameter tuning
improves \acrlong{mae} significantly. Additionally, substituting raw
station-level weather data with professionally processed commercial weather
data yields no significant predictive advantage.
These findings provide actionable guidance for the industry:
respectable forecasting accuracy can be achieved using out-of-the-box
algorithms and a constrained feature set consisting of weather,
time, and historical prices, effectively avoiding the operational
overhead associated with specialised deep
learning architectures
and exhaustive data acquisition and maintenance.

projects.title: When Burnout Enters the Mat
projects.abstract:
This thesis investigates how young female elite athletes in a Danish martial arts club experience burnout and how this phenomenon manifests, with particular focus on relational and contextual factors. The study is grounded in a hermeneutic epistemological approach and conducted as a qualitative case study inspired by reflexive thematic analysis. The empirical material consists of semi-structured interviews, questionnaires, workshop-based field notes, and initial dialogues with the club’s management. Based on the Holistic Ecological Approach (HEA), burnout is analysed as a phenomenon that emerges through the interaction of individual, relational, and structural factors within the talent development environment.
The analysis shows that burnout appears as a complex, dynamic, and recurring phenomenon that develops through a persistent imbalance between high performance demands and limited resources. The findings indicate that performance pressure is internalised by the athletes and closely linked to their sense of self-worth, resulting in self-criticism and difficulties coping with failure. At the same time, relational dynamics play a central role, particularly within the coach–athlete relationship, where a mismatch is identified between the support athletes seek and the support provided. Burnout also appears as a socially embedded phenomenon, in which group dynamics and a shared performance culture can both amplify and buffer strain. Furthermore, the analysis demonstrates that structural and cultural conditions within the environment – including implicit success criteria, a strong performance-oriented culture, and limited support structures – scontribute to an individualisation of burnout and a lack of collective approaches to managing strain.
The thesis therefore concludes that burnout cannot be understood as an individual problem, but must be approached as a relational and contextual phenomenon. Based on these findings, the study highlights the need to develop talent environments in which well-being and performance are integrated through clear communication, strengthened support structures, and a more collective approach to managing mental strain.

projects.title: Greatest Credible Draught: Analyzing AIS Data to Improve Bathymetric Models
projects.abstract: Bathymetric charts are expensive to create and maintain, but are necessary for safe navigation at sea. Outdated or incorrect measurements can result in vessel groundings of varying severity. Vessel draught reported by Automatic Identification System (AIS) transponders, it is possible to calculate a lower bound on depth. However, the data sent with AIS is not validated, and may have errors. It is important that the input AIS dataset is large, such that each cell has several visitors,which in turn means more draught measurements to ensure quality of the output. We propose a system, that for each grid cell, is able to calculate the greatest credible draught, i.e., the maximum draught, that satisfies a given credibility threshold. The system models trajectories as continuously moving vessels and, where possible,uses vessels physical dimensions to maximize the number of cells visited. The system should be capable of working with a large dataset. Therefore, we focus on building a performant system by using DuckDB and speed up techniques, such as indexes and caching. The input data consists of an AIS dataset and the Danish Depth Model (DDM), a gridded bathymetric model. A subset of the DDM is used as the ground truth for depth measurements. The measures in the DDM span more than a century, not all values are up to date. We test our system in areas with different characteristics, ranging from areas with good depth measurements and trustworthy vessels to areas with shallow waters and low traffic. With a credibility threshold of 0.7, the system is able to reduce the number of cells contradicting the DDM compared to selecting the maximum draught. Specifically we find an area of size approximately equal to 1.96km2 near Aalborg whose draught conflicts with the DDM.

projects.title: CellString: Optimising Query Performance for AIS Trajectories in Columnar Storage
projects.abstract: The Automatic Identification System (AIS) generates massive spatiotemporal datasets, but traditional query processing using LineString geometries and R-tree spatial indexes is ineffective due to highly overlapping Minimum Bounding Rectangles (MBRs). We present a columnar adaptation of CellString, a cell-based data type that is used to represent vessel trajectories and stops as contiguous sequences of cells. Using the Web Mercator XYZ tiling scheme, geographic coordinates are transformed into one-dimensional, bit-encoded quadkeys. This encoding natively preserves spatial locality, allowing DuckDB to execute zonemap pruning during table scans without relying on secondary spatial indexing. Furthermore, we extend the CellString datatype by assigning entry and exit timestamps to each cell and restructuring the physical layout to an unnested columnar format. This replaces computationally expensive geometric evaluations with parallelisable integer joins. Experiments are performed on a real-world Danish AIS dataset with more than 1.8 billion AIS points, where we compare the CellString implementation against LineString across spatial, temporal, and spatio-temporal range queries. Results show that CellString queries are strongly driven by selectivity: significant speedup is achieved for selective spatial and spatio-temporal workloads, especially in low-traffic regions and narrow time windows, while less selective queries produce larger intermediate results, which reduces the advantage over LineString queries. Furthermore, experiments show that CellString queries can achieve super-linear parallelisation. Case studies demonstrate the analytical efficiency of CellString by achieving significant speedups in transit route queries, enabling fine-grained spatial coverage queries of the Danish Exclusive Economic Zone, and providing finer spatio-temporal selectivity compared to LineString. Finally, CellString tables can be fine-tuned to either spatial or temporal workload based on row order, i.e. the order in which rows of a table are sorted.
